```python
async def chat_completions(request: Request):
    body = await request.json()
    model = body.get("model", "mock-model")
    return {
        "id": "chatcmpl-mock-0001",
        "object": "chat.completion",
        "created": int(time.time()),
        "model": model,
        "choices": [
            {
                "index": 0,
                "message": {"role": "assistant", "content": "pong again"},
                "finish_reason": "stop",
                "logprobs": None,
            }
        ],
        "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 10, "completion_tokens": 3, "total_tokens": 13},
    }
```
 
**Proxy config** (`repro_config.yaml`), started with `litellm --config repro_config.yaml --port 4000 --detailed_debug`:
```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mock-gpt
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/mock-gpt
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:8811/v1
      api_key: sk-fake-local-key   # not a real credential
 
litellm_settings:
  callbacks:
    - "code_interpreter_interception"
  code_interpreter_interception_params:
    sandbox_tool_name: mock-sandbox
 
sandbox_tools:
  - sandbox_tool_name: mock-sandbox
    litellm_params:
      sandbox_provider: e2b
      # api_key / api_base intentionally omitted: both are optional here
      # (verified in litellm/sandbox/sandbox_tools.py::_iter_valid_tools),
      # and the sandbox is never actually created in this repro since the
      # model never calls the tool.
 
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-repro-master-key  # not a real credential
```
 
**Request #1 — baseline, no streaming, same tool attached (works fine):**
```
$ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-master-key" \
  -d '{"model":"mock-gpt","stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"tools":[{"type":"code_interpreter","container":{"type":"auto"}}]}' \
  -w "\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}\n"
 
{"id":"chatcmpl-mock-0001","created":1787247405,"model":"mock-gpt","object":"chat.completion","choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"content":"pong again","role":"assistant","provider_specific_fields":{"refusal":null}},"provider_specific_fields":{}}],"usage":{"completion_tokens":3,"prompt_tokens":10,"total_tokens":13}}
HTTP_STATUS:200
```
 
**Request #2 — identical, only `stream: true` added (fails):**
```
$ curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-repro-master-key" \
  -d '{"model":"mock-gpt","stream":true,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ping"}],"tools":[{"type":"code_interpreter","container":{"type":"auto"}}]}' \
  -w "\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}\n"
 
{"error":{"message":"'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got ModelResponseStream","type":"None","param":"None","code":"500"}}
HTTP_STATUS:500
```
 
**Matching server-side traceback** (`--detailed_debug` output from the same run):
```
File ".../litellm/proxy/utils.py", line 2774, in async_post_call_streaming_iterator_hook
    async for chunk in current_response:
File ".../litellm/proxy/utils.py", line 1653, in _wrap_streaming_iterator_with_enrichment
    async for chunk in gen:
File ".../litellm/proxy/hooks/responses_id_security.py", line 267, in async_post_call_streaming_iterator_hook
    async for chunk in response:
TypeError: 'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got ModelResponseStream
```
 
Only `/v1/chat/completions` has been verified. `code_interpreter_interception` appears to share its agentic-loop plumbing with the `/v1/responses` surface (there's a shared "chat completion agentic surface" concept internally), so `/v1/responses` may well be affected too, but I have not confirmed that independently — flagging it as a suspicion, not a claim.
 
(As a side note: `sandbox_tools` only needs `sandbox_tool_name` + `sandbox_provider` to be valid — `api_key`/`api_base` are optional and, in this particular bug, never read at all, since the sandbox is never created. So this repro says nothing about self-hosted/alternative `e2b`-compatible endpoints; it reproduces purely against the stock `sandbox_provider: e2b` config path.)
 
#### Part B — cache corruption (from a production incident, real provider, not independently reproduced by me)
 
This was hit against a real model (`gpt-5.6-terra`) behind the same proxy setup (`litellm_settings.callbacks` including `code_interpreter_interception`, plus response caching enabled). A later request landed on a cache entry and failed with:
 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_response_utils/convert_dict_to_response.py", line 646, in convert_to_model_response_object
    tool_calls = choice["message"].get("tool_calls", None)
                 ~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: 'message'
 
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
 
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../litellm/router.py", line 6349, in async_function_with_retries
    response = await self.make_call(original_function, *args, **kwargs)
  ...
  File ".../litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_response_utils/convert_dict_to_response.py", line 891, in convert_to_model_response_object
    raise Exception(f"Invalid response object {traceback.format_exc()}\n\nreceived_args={received_args}")
 
received_args={'response_object': {'id': 'gen-1787237427-yq76GvhhU7FpBeG5sWa0', 'created': 1787237428, 'model': 'gpt-5.6-terra', 'object': 'chat.completion.chunk', 'system_fingerprint': None, 'choices': [{'finish_reason': 'stop', 'index': 0, 'delta': {'provider_specific_fields': {'refusal': None}, 'content': 'pong again', 'role': 'assistant', 'function_call': None, 'tool_calls': None, 'audio': None}, 'logprobs': None}], 'provider_specific_fields': None, 'usage': {'completion_tokens': 6, 'prompt_tokens': 87, 'total_tokens': 93, 'completion_tokens_details': None, 'prompt_tokens_details': {'audio_tokens': None, 'cached_tokens': 0, 'text_tokens': None, 'image_tokens': None, 'video_tokens': None}}}, 'model_response_object': ModelResponse(id='chatcmpl-f88fa605-68e4-4438-b3bf-120b5f219216', created=1787246...
```
 
Note the cached `response_object` has `'object': 'chat.completion.chunk'` and a `'delta'` field on its choice — i.e. it's a streaming-chunk shape, not a full `chat.completion` response, even though this was served as a cached "final" response. This is consistent with Part A: whatever object ends up satisfying neither "full response" nor "real async stream" is exactly the kind of object that gets read back later and blows up `convert_to_model_response_object` the same way.
 
I was not able to cleanly reproduce this half in an isolated local setup (my attempts to combine a local in-memory cache with the streaming request above ran into an unrelated hung-connection issue in that environment), so I'm including it as an as-reported production trace rather than an independently-verified repro. Happy to try again with guidance on which caching backend/config is most likely to hit this cleanly.
 
---
 
### Suggested fix direction (not required reading, just my read of the code)
 
The place that seems to produce the non-iterable object is whatever helper converts a completed (non-streaming) `ModelResponse` back into a "fake stream" for a client that originally asked for `stream: true` — it looks like it returns a single streaming-chunk object rather than something with `__aiter__`. Anything downstream that does `async for chunk in response` (proxy-level post-call streaming hooks, in this case) then fails immediately, and anything that caches "the response" for this call ends up caching that same chunk-shaped object instead of a full response.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.97.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This is a clear bug: a specific, well-documented feature combination (code_interpreter_interception + stream:true) crashes with an unhandled TypeError, breaking the request entirely with no workaround other than not streaming. There's also a secondary, related issue where a malformed cache entry can be left behind, causing later unrelated requests to fail with a KeyError. This is not a docs issue since the code violates the expected/reasonable behavior (streaming should either work or fail gracefully with a clear 4xx), and it's not a question since the reporter is not asking how to do something but reporting broken behavior with detailed reproduction steps. The cache corruption aspect is especially severe since it can silently propagate failures to unrelated requests. This affects a shared code path (streaming + interception) that likely affects many users using code_interpreter tooling with streaming, and there's no built-in workaround besides disabling streaming (a partial workaround, not full). Given the crash is a hard TypeError with clear reproduction, and the cache corruption risk affects unrelated future requests (data integrity concern), urgency is elevated. It doesn't quite rise to "broken for most users on a current release" since it only affects a specific combination (streaming + code_interpreter tool), but it does affect the shared core response-caching path when it corrupts cache entries, which can have knock-on effects for other requests too. This warrants P1: a widely-used integration path (streaming) combined with a specific but growing feature is broken, and the cache corruption issue is a correctness/data integrity bug affecting unrelated requests. Needs human because: it's P1, requires reproduction confirmation for the cache corruption piece (reporter states "not yet independently reproduced by me"), and requires judgement on the right architectural fix (support streaming vs reject with 4xx) - a product-direction question.

items.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek thinking-by-default models + tools: _fill_reasoning_content guard never fires without explicit reasoning params, upstream 400
items.body:
## What happened?

DeepSeek V4 models (`deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek-v4-flash`) run **thinking mode by default server-side**. In a multi-turn tool-calling loop, DeepSeek's API requires `reasoning_content` to be passed back on assistant messages, otherwise it returns:

```
400 {"error":{"message":"The `reasoning_content` in the thinking mode must be passed back to the API.", "type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

LiteLLM already handles this: `DeepSeekChatConfig._fill_reasoning_content` (added for #28045) promotes `provider_specific_fields.reasoning_content` or injects a minimal placeholder. However, the gate that decides whether to run it assumes thinking is **opt-in**:

```python
# litellm/llms/deepseek/chat/transformation.py
def _thinking_mode_active(self, model: str, optional_params: dict) -> bool:
    return (
        supports_reasoning(model=model, custom_llm_provider="deepseek")
        and (optional_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type") == "enabled"
    )
```

When the request carries **no** `thinking`/`reasoning_effort` at all — the common case for a router/proxy deployment that doesn't inject reasoning params — the guard is `False`, `_fill_reasoning_content` never runs, and the DeepSeek API rejects every second call of a tool loop with the 400 above. The model was in thinking mode the whole time; the request just never said so.

The guard's opt-in assumption is documented in its own comment ("preventing spurious injection on models like deepseek-v3.2 that support thinking as opt-in but not always-on") — correct for opt-in models, wrong for thinking-by-default models.

## Reproduction (litellm proxy v1.96.2 or SDK)

```python
import litellm

TOOLS = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_time",
          "description": "Get current time",
          "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}]
MSGS = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What time is it? Use the tool."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "",
     "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function",
                     "function": {"name": "get_time", "arguments": "{}"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "14:32 UTC"},
]

# FAILS with the 400 above — no reasoning params, guard never fires:
litellm.completion(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", messages=MSGS, tools=TOOLS)

# WORKS — reasoning_effort maps to thinking:{"type":"enabled"}, guard fires,
# _fill_reasoning_content runs:
litellm.completion(model="deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro", messages=MSGS, tools=TOOLS,
                   reasoning_effort="high")
```

Both verified against the live DeepSeek API through a litellm proxy v1.96.2.

## Expected behavior

For models whose thinking mode is on by default, `_fill_reasoning_content` should run unless the request **explicitly disables** thinking (`thinking: {"type": "disabled"}` / `reasoning_effort: "none"` — explicit disable works today and needs no fill: verified that a disabled-thinking tool loop passes).

## Proposed fix

Make the default-on property data-driven and extend the guard:

1. Add a capability flag in the model cost map for thinking-by-default models
   (e.g. `"thinking_by_default": true` on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`,
   `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, and other always-on reasoning models).
2. Change the guard to:

```python
def _thinking_mode_active(self, model: str, optional_params: dict) -> bool:
    if not supports_reasoning(model=model, custom_llm_provider="deepseek"):
        return False
    thinking = (optional_params.get("thinking") or {}).get("type")
    if thinking == "enabled":
        return True
    if thinking == "disabled":
        return False
    return thinking_by_default(model)   # <- new: no explicit choice on the wire
```

This keeps the #28045 behavior intact for opt-in models (deepseek-v3.2) and
closes the hole for default-on models.

## Workaround we're using today

Pin `reasoning_effort` on the proxy deployment so the guard fires (wire-neutral:
every non-`"none"` value maps to plain `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}`, which is
already the server default):

```yaml
- model_name: deepseek-v4-pro
  litellm_params:
    model: deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro
    api_key: os.environ/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
    reasoning_effort: "high"
```

## Environment

- litellm v1.96.2 (proxy, `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.96.2`)
- Models: `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`
- Surfaced at scale behind a router where client requests carry no reasoning
  params (the deployment decides) — every tool-using turn 400s on its second call.

gold.rationale: This is a clear bug: the code's documented intent (fill reasoning_content for models in thinking mode to satisfy DeepSeek's API contract) is violated for thinking-by-default models, causing every second turn of a tool-calling loop to 400 against a real upstream provider. It's not a docs issue since the code itself has the wrong logic/gate, not just a documentation mismatch. It reproducibly breaks a widely-used provider (DeepSeek) in a common deployment pattern (router/proxy without explicit reasoning params), affecting all tool-calling users of these models. There is a workaround (pinning reasoning_effort on the proxy deployment), which is somewhat painful since it requires deployment-level config changes and doesn't fix default behavior for SDK users who don't set it. Given a widely-used provider integration is broken for a common use case (tool loops), this warrants P1, but the presence of a viable workaround pulls it down one level to P2. This is a well-specified bug report with clear reproduction, proposed fix, and root cause identified — a maintainer can route this to the deepseek transformation module without further discussion, though the actual code change should be reviewed by someone familiar with the reasoning_content contract. Given the clear reproduction and proposed fix, it doesn't need human triage for information-gathering purposes, but since it involves a provider integration bug with real business impact, and the fix touches capability flags in the model cost map, it's borderline. I'll set needs_human to false since this is a well-specified bug with clear repro and fix path.

items.title: [Bug]: Background health checks load the entire (unbounded) LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable into every worker each cycle → excessive/near-OOM memory + DB storms at scale
items.body:
## What happened?

Two independent defects in the background health-check loop combine to storm the database every cycle (default 15 min) when running `use_shared_health_check: true` with multiple workers:

**Bug 1 — DB persistence is not leader-gated:**
`SharedHealthCheckManager` correctly gates the **probing** step (only the lock-holder sends health-check requests to LLM providers). But after probing, `_run_background_health_check()` unconditionally calls `_schedule_background_health_check_db_save()` on **every worker** (line ~3499 of `proxy_server.py`). Each worker runs `get_all_latest_health_checks()` — a `SELECT DISTINCT ON` full-table scan — plus per-model INSERTs. With N workers this multiplies DB load by N every cycle.

**Bug 2 — HealthCheckTable is append-only with no retention:**
`save_health_check_result()` in `PrismaClient` uses `.create()` (INSERT). There is no upsert and no pruning. The table grows unbounded. Because `get_all_latest_health_checks()` uses `DISTINCT ON (model_id, model_name)` ordered by `checked_at DESC`, Postgres must scan **all rows** to find the latest per model — there is no loose index-scan optimization for `DISTINCT ON`.

**Combined impact at scale:**
In our production environment (360 models, ~10 workers, 15-min cycle), the table grew to **3.9 million rows** in 64 days. `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` of `get_all_latest_health_checks()` shows:

- **4.18 seconds** execution time
- **~31 GB** buffer traffic (index + heap)
- Scans all 3.9M rows to return 360

When ~10 workers run this simultaneously against a near-idle database (we use Aurora Serverless v2 with auto-scaling), it triggers a cold scale-up to max capacity, which causes connection churn, severs query-engine connections across all tasks, health saves fail, deployments get marked unavailable, and the proxy returns `No deployments available` 500s. We observed a **20.6% 5xx rate** during a 25-minute incident window.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure LiteLLM proxy with:
   ```yaml
   general_settings:
     use_shared_health_check: true
     background_health_checks: true
     health_check_interval: 900  # 15 min
   ```
2. Deploy with multiple workers (e.g. 4+ Gunicorn workers or multiple pods behind a load balancer) and 100+ models in config.
3. Let the proxy run for several weeks.
4. Observe `LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable` row count growing linearly (models × cycles × workers per cycle):
   ```sql
   SELECT count(*) FROM "LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable";
   -- After 64 days with 360 models, 10 workers: ~3.9M rows
   ```
5. Observe that **every worker** calls `get_all_latest_health_checks()` each cycle, not just the leader:
   ```sql
   -- Proof of leaderless fan-out: distinct checked_by values within a single cycle
   SELECT checked_at, checked_by, count(*)
   FROM "LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable"
   WHERE checked_at > now() - interval '20 minutes'
   GROUP BY checked_at, checked_by
   ORDER BY checked_at DESC;
   -- Returns rows for EACH pod writing the same models <60s apart
   ```
6. At sufficient table size, the `DISTINCT ON` read becomes multi-second, and concurrent execution from N workers causes DB saturation / connection exhaustion.

## Relevant log output

```
# EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the DISTINCT ON read (3.9M rows, 360 models):
Unique  (cost=0.56..2847163.44 rows=360 width=1389) (actual time=0.194..4183.021 rows=360 loops=1)
  ->  Index Scan using ... on "LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable" (actual time=0.193..3922.574 rows=3900000 loops=1)
Planning Time: 0.422 ms
Execution Time: 4183.541 ms
Buffers: shared hit=31457280
```

## Root Cause in Code

**`proxy_server.py` ~L3498-3505** — `_schedule_background_health_check_db_save()` is called unconditionally regardless of whether this worker was the health-check leader:
```python
# Save background health checks to database (non-blocking)
_schedule_background_health_check_db_save(
    prisma_client,
    shared_health_manager,
    _llm_model_list,
    healthy_endpoints,
    unhealthy_endpoints,
)
```

**`utils.py` ~L5138** — `save_health_check_result()` uses `.create()` (INSERT), never upserts or prunes:
```python
return await HealthCheckRepository(self).table.create(data=health_check_data)
```

**`utils.py` ~L5180-5187** — `get_all_latest_health_checks()` does `DISTINCT ON` over the full table:
```python
return await HealthCheckRepository(self).table.find_many(
    distinct=["model_id", "model_name"],
    order=[
        {"model_id": "asc"},
        {"model_name": "asc"},
        {"checked_at": "desc"},
    ],
)
```

## Suggested Fix

**Short-term (two changes):**

1. **Leader-gate the DB persistence:** `SharedHealthCheckManager` already elects a leader for probing. Expose an `is_current_pod_leader` flag (set True when the pod acquires the lock or falls back to local probe; reset to False on cache hit). Gate `_schedule_background_health_check_db_save()` on it so exactly one pod does the read + write per cycle. When `shared_health_manager is None`, preserve the existing per-pod behavior.

2. **Add retention pruning:** After a successful save, the leader prunes rows older than a retention window (e.g. 7 days) via a batched, bounded DELETE. This caps the `DISTINCT ON` scan cost at O(recent rows) instead of O(all history). Batching (e.g. 10k rows per pass, max 50 passes) avoids long locks on the first run against a large backlog.

**Long-term (architectural):**

Replace the append-only `LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable` with a **one-row-per-model upsert** design (a `LiteLLM_HealthCheckLatest` table with `model_id` as primary key, upserted each cycle). This makes the "latest per model" read O(N models) — a simple `SELECT *` — instead of `DISTINCT ON` over unbounded history. History can be kept in the existing table with retention, or dropped entirely.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

## What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.94.3

gold.rationale: This is a well-documented bug: the background health-check code violates the intended leader-election contract (only one worker should persist/probe), causing unbounded table growth and DB storms. This is a "behaves differently from documented/expected behaviour" issue with clear root cause, reproduction steps, EXPLAIN ANALYZE evidence, and production incident data (20.6% 5xx rate). It affects the shared core health-check path used by any multi-worker proxy deployment with use_shared_health_check enabled, causing DB saturation, connection exhaustion, and 500s ("No deployments available") for many users at scale. No workaround is stated other than the suggested code fix (leader-gating + retention). Given it affects the shared core path and causes broad production outages at scale, this warrants P0/P1 severity; since it's not universally broken for all users (only multi-worker + scale + time), but has significant blast radius affecting a widely-used feature (shared health checks) and causing outages, P1 is appropriate. It requires maintainer judgement to decide on the fix approach (leader gating vs table redesign) and to confirm/reproduce at scale, so needs_human=true.

items.title: is the websearch tool interception intended to work this way?
items.body: I configured websearch interception using the info at `https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/tutorials/claude_code_websearch` with serper. THen i ran a search. As you can see it says `Did 0 Search`. But the results are correct and serper credits are consumed (with the same search terms being shown on serper's dashboard). I am only concerned about the '0' search indication. Is this the expected behavior?

gold.rationale: The user reports that the websearch interception feature performs actual searches (results correct, serper credits consumed, search terms logged on serper's dashboard) but the UI/response metadata incorrectly reports "Did 0 Search". This is a discrepancy between actual behavior (search executed) and reported/displayed behavior (count shows 0), indicating incorrect accounting/reporting in the websearch_interception module rather than a documentation issue or a how-to question—the user explicitly flags this as unexpected behavior. This fits the bug category, similar to "incorrect cost or token accounting" style issues, just applied to search count reporting. It affects a specific integration path (websearch interception with Claude Code/serper), not the shared core path, and a workaround exists (functionality still works correctly despite wrong count), so this is a narrower issue affecting a subset of users. This warrants P2 urgency. Since it's a clear, reproducible bug with a screenshot and specific repro steps pointing to a specific module (websearch_interception), it can be routed without further clarification needed from a maintainer.

items.title: [Bug]: generateContent bridge drops functionDeclarations.parameters, so tool schemas are silently lost for non-Gemini providers
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

When a Gemini-native `generateContent` request is served by a model whose deployment points at a non-Gemini provider, the tool parameter schema is dropped. The function name and description reach the upstream model; the arguments schema does not, so the model calls the function with empty or invented arguments.

The request succeeds, nothing is logged as an error, and the caller gets a well-formed `functionCall` with the wrong `args`.

The bridge that converts a `generateContent` body into a chat-completions body only reads `functionDeclarations[].parametersJsonSchema`. That is the field `gemini-cli` sends. The `google-genai` SDKs serialize tool schemas to `functionDeclarations[].parameters` instead, and there is no branch for it.

I confirmed what the SDK puts on the wire by pointing `google-genai` 1.69.0 at a local HTTP listener. Both idiomatic ways of declaring a tool produce `parameters`:

```python
fd = types.FunctionDeclaration(
    name="get_weather", description="Get weather",
    parameters=types.Schema(type="OBJECT",
        properties={"city": types.Schema(type="STRING", description="City name")},
        required=["city"]))
```

```json
{"functionDeclarations":[{"name":"get_weather","description":"Get weather",
  "parameters":{"type":"OBJECT","properties":{"city":{"type":"STRING","description":"City name"}},"required":["city"]}}]}
```

Passing a plain Python callable as a tool produces `parameters` as well. I could not get the SDK to emit `parametersJsonSchema` through either path.

Expected: a tool declared with `parameters` reaches the upstream model with its schema intact, exactly as one declared with `parametersJsonSchema` does today.

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app uses the Google GenAI SDK against the proxy gets function calls back with empty arguments as soon as the model name is served by a non-Gemini deployment.

1. They point their app at the proxy and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent`, where `my-model` is served by an OpenAI-compatible deployment, with one tool declared: `get_weather`, taking a required string `city`
2. They get `200` back with `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}` — the right function, no arguments
3. Their app calls `get_weather()` with no city, and either raises a `KeyError` or looks up the weather for nowhere
4. On repeated runs the model sometimes returns `{"args":{"location":"Hanoi"}}` instead — a parameter name that appears nowhere in the tool they declared
5. They point the same app at `my-gemini-model`, served by a Gemini deployment, send the identical request, and get `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"Hanoi"}}}` — so the same client code works on one model and silently misbehaves on another

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same request returns the arguments the tool declared, whichever provider serves the model.

1. They point their app at the proxy and send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent`, where `my-model` is served by an OpenAI-compatible deployment, with one tool declared: `get_weather`, taking a required string `city`
2. They get `200` back with `{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"Hanoi"}}}`
3. Their app calls `get_weather(city="Hanoi")` and returns the right weather
4. Repeated runs return the same `city` argument every time
5. Pointing the same app at `my-gemini-model` returns the identical result, so behaviour no longer depends on which provider backs the model name

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: my-model
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o
      api_base: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1   # any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_COMPAT_KEY

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
```

Version: `v1.97.0` (`ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.97.0`, `importlib.metadata.version("litellm")` reports `1.97.0`)

Command — tool declared with `parameters`, which is what the SDK sends:

```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do
curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent" \
 -H "x-goog-api-key: sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "contents":[{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"What is the weather in Hanoi? Use the tool."}]}],
  "tools":[{"functionDeclarations":[{"name":"get_weather","description":"Get the weather for a city",
    "parameters":{"type":"OBJECT","properties":{"city":{"type":"STRING","description":"City name"}},"required":["city"]}}]}]}'
echo; done
```

Output — the model is called with no arguments on every run:

```
{"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0,"safetyRatings":[]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":49,"candidatesTokenCount":11,"totalTokenCount":60}}
{"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0,"safetyRatings":[]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":49,"candidatesTokenCount":11,"totalTokenCount":60}}
{"candidates":[{"content":{"parts":[{"functionCall":{"name":"get_weather","args":{}}}],"role":"model"},"finishReason":"STOP","index":0,"safetyRatings":[]}],"usageMetadata":{"promptTokenCount":49,"candidatesTokenCount":11,"totalTokenCount":60}}
```

Control — the byte-identical schema under `parametersJsonSchema`, same proxy, same model, same prompt:

```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do
curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1beta/models/my-model:generateContent" \
 -H "x-goog-api-key: sk-1234" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "contents":[{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"What is the weather in Hanoi? Use the tool."}]}],
  "tools":[{"functionDeclarations":[{"name":"get_weather","description":"Get the weather for a city",
    "parametersJsonSchema":{"type":"OBJECT","properties":{"city":{"type":"STRING","description":"City name"}},"required":["city"]}}]}]}'
echo; done
```

Output — arguments arrive intact, so the upstream model and the provider are fine:

```
{"functionCall": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Hanoi"}}}
{"functionCall": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Hanoi"}}}
{"functionCall": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Hanoi"}}}
```

Note on the prompt token counts: 49 in the failing case against 59 in the control — the schema is missing from what leaves the proxy, not merely ignored by the model.

The same difference shows up against a Gemini-backed deployment, which takes the native path rather than the bridge and returns `{"city":"Hanoi"}` for both field spellings.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.97.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: The bridge converting generateContent requests to chat-completions format only reads functionDeclarations[].parametersJsonSchema, missing the parameters field that both idiomatic SDK usages (google-genai) actually send. This causes tool schemas to be silently dropped for non-Gemini providers, resulting in empty or hallucinated function arguments. This is a clear behavioral bug (code violates the expected/documented contract of passing tool schemas through), well reproduced with curl commands and control comparison. It affects any non-Gemini provider deployment behind the generateContent bridge, which is a widely-used cross-provider path (affects all OpenAI-compatible and other non-Gemini providers, a core path), and there's no workaround for SDK users since the SDK itself emits `parameters` not `parametersJsonSchema`. This silently produces wrong output without error, which is a correctness/reliability issue impacting a broad swath of users of the Gemini-compatible endpoint for non-Gemini providers.

items.title: [Bug]: search router silently drops provider-specific litellm_params from yaml search_tools entries
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

When a `search_tools` entry in the proxy config carries provider-specific keys in its `litellm_params` (for example `tool_name` for the agentcore provider, or `aws_access_key_id` / `aws_secret_access_key` overrides), those keys are silently dropped. The search router forwards only `search_provider`, `api_key`, and `api_base` from the tool's `litellm_params` to the underlying search call (`SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` in `litellm/router_utils/search_api_router.py`), so every other key is ignored with no warning, no boot error, and no request-time error

Expected: either every `litellm_params` key is forwarded to the provider (the way `model_list` entries forward their `litellm_params` to completion calls), or the proxy rejects unknown keys loudly at boot so an admin finds out their knob is dead

The same keys do work when passed per request in the body or set via provider env vars (for agentcore, `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME`), which is how the guard behind `tool_name` stays reachable. Only the yaml path is dead. The agentcore example config was corrected in #36331 to stop advertising the yaml knobs; this issue tracks fixing the plumbing itself, which affects all search providers

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a proxy admin whose AgentCore gateway target has a custom name configures it in yaml and every search silently uses the wrong tool name

1. They add a `search_tools` entry with `search_provider: agentcore`, their gateway `api_base`, and `tool_name: MyTarget___WebSearch` in `litellm_params`, then start the proxy; boot succeeds with no warning
2. They send POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search with `{"query": "latest AI developments", "max_results": 5}`
3. The request goes out with the default `web-search-tool___WebSearch` instead of their configured name; on a gateway whose target really has a custom name this comes back as an MCP tool-not-found error, and on a gateway that also has a default-named target it silently searches through the wrong one
4. Nothing in the response or the logs says their yaml `tool_name` was ignored

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same config works, or fails loudly

1. They add the same `search_tools` entry and start the proxy
2. They send the same POST http://litellm-domain/v1/search/agentcore-search request
3. The request goes out with `MyTarget___WebSearch` and returns results from their target, or, if the key is deliberately unsupported, the proxy refuses to boot naming the unsupported key

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with (proxy booted from PR #36331 at commit `70a4f9a73aabd327b9c06e52bf5d47b437b76430`; the router file involved is untouched by that PR and identical on `litellm_internal_staging`):

```yaml
search_tools:
  - search_tool_name: agentcore-badtool
    litellm_params:
      search_provider: agentcore
      api_base: https://litellm-qa-agentcore-tez4ymmxfc.gateway.bedrock-agentcore.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/mcp
      tool_name: my-target___ListFiles
```

The agentcore provider rejects any `tool_name` not ending in `___WebSearch`, so this request must fail. Instead it returns HTTP 200 with real web results, against a real AgentCore gateway:

```
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:26793/v1/search/agentcore-badtool \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -d '{"query": "anything", "max_results": 2}' -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}\n'

{"results":[{"title":"Anything","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anything", ...}],"object":"search"}
HTTP 200
```

The proxy debug log shows the outgoing JSON-RPC call used the default tool name, not the configured one, proving the yaml value never reached the provider:

```
-d '{'jsonrpc': '2.0', 'id': 1, 'method': 'tools/call', 'params': {'name': 'web-search-tool___WebSearch', 'arguments': {'query': 'anything', 'maxResults': 2}}}'
```

Control showing the guard itself works when the value arrives via env var: rebooting the same proxy with `AGENTCORE_SEARCH_TOOL_NAME=my-target___ListFiles` exported makes the same request refuse with

```
Invalid AgentCore search tool_name 'my-target___ListFiles': must end with '___WebSearch' (a web-search connector tool). Other gateway tools cannot be invoked through this provider.
```

Fix sketch: forward the tool's full `litellm_params` (minus `search_provider`, which becomes the positional provider) as kwargs from `SearchAPIRouter.async_search_with_fallbacks_helper` into the search call, mirroring how `model_list` `litellm_params` flow into completion calls, with request-body params winning over yaml on key collisions. Needs a check across all search providers that previously-ignored yaml keys don't change behavior for existing configs

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

litellm_internal_staging at 2059033352de (also present at PR #36331 tip 70a4f9a7)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: The search router only forwards search_provider, api_key, and api_base from search_tools' litellm_params, silently dropping provider-specific keys like tool_name. This causes documented/expected behavior (yaml-configured knobs) to not work, with no error, and can even route requests through the wrong tool silently — a clear behavioral bug versus documented/expected contract (mirrors model_list litellm_params forwarding). It's not a security vulnerability itself (no exploit path stated), not a docs issue (code behavior is wrong, not just described wrong), and not a pure feature since the capability is meant to already exist per config schema. This affects all search providers uniformly (shared plumbing in SearchAPIRouter), which is the core path for the search feature — a subset of proxy users (those using search_tools yaml config) but touches the shared router code for all providers. Given it silently produces wrong/misleading results (potentially querying wrong data source) with no workaround other than per-request params or env vars (a partial workaround exists per issue), and affects a narrower feature path (search proxy add-on, not mainstream completion) but "affects all search providers" broadening scope. Given the workaround (env var or per-request) mentioned, apply the workaround modifier to lower one level from P1 to P2. This needs human judgement to decide the intended fix approach (forward all vs validate at boot) and to verify impact across providers, so needs_human=true.

items.title: cache_control_injection_points has no equivalent for OpenAI prompt_cache_breakpoint on OpenAI-compatible targets
items.body:
## Summary

`cache_control_injection_points` (via `AnthropicCacheControlHook`, introduced in #9996 and extended to the `/v1/messages` path in #30341/#30615 for issue #30293) lets an admin configure, at the deployment level, where a stable-prefix cache boundary should be placed. Today this hook only ever produces Anthropic-shaped `cache_control` blocks. There is no equivalent path that emits OpenAI's GPT-5.6+ `prompt_cache_breakpoint` (per content block) plus `prompt_cache_options` (request-level `mode`/`ttl`) when the deployment actually routes to an OpenAI-compatible target.

## Why this matters

OpenAI's GPT-5.6+ caching model supports the same concept — an explicit marker on the last content block of a reusable prefix — as `prompt_cache_breakpoint`, combined with `prompt_cache_options.mode` to control whether the automatic implicit breakpoint stays active alongside it. This is functionally the same admin intent `cache_control_injection_points` already expresses for Anthropic, just via a different wire format on a different provider.

Without this, admins running mixed model fleets (Anthropic + OpenAI GPT-5.6 deployments behind the same proxy config pattern) have a working, centrally-configured caching primitive for Anthropic-backed deployments and *no* equivalent centrally-configured primitive for OpenAI-backed ones — caching for OpenAI targets is left entirely to either the client (which, for Anthropic-shaped clients like Claude Code, has no notion of `prompt_cache_breakpoint` at all — see openai/codex#35300 for the same gap in another Anthropic-shaped client, Codex CLI) or to OpenAI's default implicit-mode caching, which the docs note is exact-match-only on GPT-5.6+ and does not do the longest-matching-prefix fallback earlier models had.

This means a stable prefix (e.g. a large system prompt + tool definitions, sent identically by an Anthropic-shaped client on every turn) that would reliably cache on Anthropic never gets the same reliable treatment on OpenAI targets, purely because of a proxy-side config gap rather than a client or model limitation.

## Request

When a deployment configured with `cache_control_injection_points` routes to an OpenAI-compatible target that supports explicit prompt-cache breakpoints (GPT-5.6+), translate the configured injection point(s) into:
- a `prompt_cache_breakpoint: {"mode": "explicit"}` marker on the corresponding outgoing content block, and
- `prompt_cache_options` at the request root (at minimum enabling explicit mode; `ttl` currently only supports `"30m"` per OpenAI's docs so may not need to be configurable yet).

Leaving the specific implementation approach (extend `AnthropicCacheControlHook` with provider-aware branching vs. a new parallel hook) to maintainer judgment — filing this to capture the gap, not to prescribe the fix.

## Related
- #30293 / #30341 / #30615 — established the pattern this issue is asking to extend to OpenAI-compatible targets
- #32669 — adds `prompt_cache_breakpoint` as a passthrough param for GPT-5.6 models (request-shape plumbing this issue would build on)
- openai/codex#35300 — the same underlying gap (no way to emit `prompt_cache_breakpoint`) from the client side, for a different Anthropic-shaped client

gold.rationale: This is a well-specified feature request: extend the existing cache_control_injection_points config to also emit OpenAI's prompt_cache_breakpoint/prompt_cache_options for OpenAI-compatible targets. The functionality does not exist yet - it's asking for new behavior, not a bug or docs issue. The reporter explicitly frames it as a gap to capture, not prescribing implementation, and leaves the approach to maintainer judgment - this is clearly a feature request. There's no evidence of multiple users requesting this (single detailed write-up from one reporter), so per the rules it defaults to P3 despite being well-argued. It doesn't affect a widely-used provider's core path being broken (it's a missing capability, not broken behavior), and there's no regression or workaround language relevant here. This is a product-direction call (whether to build a parallel translation path for OpenAI caching) requiring maintainer judgement on implementation approach, so needs_human should be true.

items.title: [Bug]: vercel_ai_gateway streaming drops prompt_tokens_details (cached_tokens) — regression since v1.95, overcharges cache-heavy streaming workloads
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

# [Bug]: `vercel_ai_gateway` streaming drops `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` — regression since v1.95, massively overcharges cache-heavy streaming workloads

## What happened?

For `vercel_ai_gateway` models, **streaming** responses lose `prompt_tokens_details` (it comes back `null`), so LiteLLM cannot see `cached_tokens` and bills the entire prompt as fresh input. **Non-streaming** requests to the same model, same prompt, are fine (`cached_tokens` populated correctly).

This is a **regression**: it works in **v1.89.3** and is broken in **v1.95.0, v1.97.0, and v1.98.0-rc.1**.

Impact for us: a real production window billed by Vercel at **$0.50 (97% cache read)** was recorded by LiteLLM at **$3.71 (4% cache detected) → 7.4x overcharge**, because ~97% of traffic is streaming and the cache read tokens are counted as fresh input.

## How to reproduce

Config (a `vercel_ai_gateway` model with a discounted cache-read rate):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: minimax
    litellm_params:
      model: vercel_ai_gateway/minimax/minimax-m3
      api_key: os.environ/VERCEL_AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
      input_cost_per_token: 0.0000003
      output_cost_per_token: 0.0000012
      cache_read_input_token_cost: 0.00000006
```

Send the **same large prompt several times** to warm Vercel's prompt cache (vary only a short trailing user message so the client-side response cache doesn't short-circuit it), once **non-streaming** and once **streaming**:

```bash
# NON-STREAMING  -> prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens is POPULATED
curl -s $LITELLM/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"minimax","stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<large repeated prompt>"},{"role":"user","content":"reply OK 1"}]}'

# STREAMING (even with include_usage) -> prompt_tokens_details is NULL
curl -s $LITELLM/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"minimax","stream":true,"stream_options":{"include_usage":true},"messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<large repeated prompt>"},{"role":"user","content":"reply OK 2"}]}'
```

Inspect the final `usage` object of each (or the SpendLogs `metadata.usage_object`).

## Expected

Streaming `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` should be populated (as in non-streaming), so cache reads are billed at `cache_read_input_token_cost`.

## Actual

- Non-streaming: `prompt_tokens_details: {"cached_tokens": 33121, ...}` ✅ (billed at cache rate)
- Streaming: `prompt_tokens_details: null` ❌ (all tokens billed at input rate → overcharge)

Note: `stream_options.include_usage: true` **is** set and usage totals do arrive — only `prompt_tokens_details` is dropped during streamed usage reassembly.

## Version regression (reproduced with identical prompt/model, only version changed)

| LiteLLM version | non-streaming | streaming |
|---|---|---|
| v1.89.3 | cached populated ✅ | **cached populated ✅** |
| v1.95.0 | cached populated ✅ | **null ❌** |
| v1.97.0 | cached populated ✅ | **null ❌** |
| v1.98.0-rc.1 | cached populated ✅ | **null ❌** |

## Cross-check against the provider's own billing (ground truth)

Same 1-minute production window, streaming traffic:

- **Vercel AI Gateway usage log:** Input = 186,021 tokens, **Cache Read = 6,545,053 tokens (97.2% cached)**, cost **$0.50**.
- **LiteLLM (same window):** only 4% of requests had `cached_tokens` populated, recorded spend **$3.71 (7.4x)**.

So the provider **does** return cache-read usage for streaming; LiteLLM discards it on the streaming path.

## Possibly related

PR #34812 ("keep OpenAI prompt cache token details through streaming usage reassembly") appears to target this class of bug but does not cover `vercel_ai_gateway` streaming — the regression persists through v1.98.0-rc.1.

## Environment

- LiteLLM Proxy (Docker, `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:<version>`)
- Provider: `vercel_ai_gateway` (models: minimax/minimax-m3, zai/glm-5.2 — same behavior)
- Reproduced on v1.95.0, v1.97.0, v1.98.0-rc.1; **not** present on v1.89.3


### User Flow

1. Configure a vercel_ai_gateway model with cache_read_input_token_cost set.
2. Send the SAME large prompt twice (vary only a short trailing user message):
   once with "stream": false, once with "stream": true + stream_options.include_usage=true.
3. Inspect usage.prompt_tokens_details of each response.
Expected: cached_tokens populated in both.
Actual: populated in non-streaming, NULL in streaming (cache read billed as fresh input).
Regression: works in v1.89.3, broken in v1.95.0 / v1.97.0 / v1.98.0-rc.1.

### Proof the bug occurs

PROOF 1 — A/B, same prompt & model, only version/stream changed:

| LiteLLM version | non-streaming | streaming |
|-----------------|---------------|-----------|
| v1.89.3         | cached OK ✅   | cached OK ✅  |
| v1.95.0         | cached OK ✅   | NULL ❌      |
| v1.97.0         | cached OK ✅   | NULL ❌      |
| v1.98.0-rc.1    | cached OK ✅   | NULL ❌      |

Non-streaming usage_object:
  "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 33121, ...}   (billed at cache rate)
Streaming usage_object (same prompt, stream_options.include_usage=true):
  "prompt_tokens_details": null                            (all billed as fresh input)

PROOF 2 — Cross-check vs the provider's own billing log (ground truth),
same 1-minute production window, streaming traffic:

  Vercel AI Gateway usage log : Input 186,021 | Cache Read 6,545,053 (97.2% cached) | cost $0.50
  LiteLLM (same window)       : cached_tokens present in only 4% of requests | recorded spend $3.71

=> 7.4x overcharge. The provider DOES return cache-read usage for streaming;
   LiteLLM discards prompt_tokens_details on the streaming reassembly path.

PROOF 3 — Fixed by downgrading to v1.89.3 in production:
  Before (v1.97): cached populated ~2-4% of requests, $/req ~$0.06-0.12
  After  (v1.89.3): cached populated ~100% of requests, $/req dropped ~2x

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

_No response_

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.95.0 / v1.97.0 / v1.98.0-rc.1 (broken), v1.89.3 (works)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This is a clear regression: cached_tokens/prompt_tokens_details is correctly populated in non-streaming responses but dropped during streaming usage reassembly for vercel_ai_gateway, causing significant overbilling (documented 7.4x overcharge in production). The report includes detailed reproduction steps, version bisection (works in v1.89.3, broken since v1.95.0), and cross-checked evidence against provider billing logs. This matches the bug category (incorrect cost/token accounting, streaming issue) rather than a feature request. Since it's a regression affecting billing accuracy for a provider integration and affects cache-heavy streaming workloads broadly (not just this reporter's edge case), and there's no stated workaround other than downgrading to an old version (which is a workaround but painful - requires full version rollback), this warrants elevated urgency. Base urgency would be P1/P2 since it's a specific provider (not "most users") but core streaming usage reassembly logic is shared code path affecting multiple providers potentially (related to PR #34812 also referencing OpenAI). Given the regression modifier (+1 level) and the severe financial impact reproducibility, this should be P1. Needs human review is required since this is a P1 bug requiring investigation into the streaming reassembly code and confirmation of the regression's root cause and scope across providers.

items.title: additional_drop_params strips fields from message content blocks, not just top-level request params
items.body:
# Bug: `additional_drop_params` strips fields from message content blocks, not just top-level request params

## Description

`additional_drop_params` is intended to drop top-level request parameters (e.g., `thinking`, `temperature`) before they're sent to the provider. However, it also recursively strips fields with the same name from **inside message content blocks**, breaking valid conversation histories.

## Reproduction

### Config:
```yaml
- model_name: "claude-opus-5"
  litellm_params:
    model: "anthropic/claude-opus-5"
    api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
    additional_drop_params: ["thinking", "temperature", "top_p", "top_k"]
```

### Request:
```python
import litellm

response = litellm.completion(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"},
        {"role": "assistant", "content": [
            {"type": "thinking", "thinking": "The user asks about 2+2. The answer is 4."},
            {"type": "text", "text": "4"}
        ]},
        {"role": "user", "content": "And 3+3?"}
    ],
    max_tokens=100
)
```

### Expected behavior:

- The top-level `thinking` request parameter (if present) should be stripped.
- The `thinking` **field inside message content blocks** (`messages[].content[].thinking`) should be left intact — it's part of the conversation history, not a request parameter.

### Actual behavior:

The `thinking` field is stripped from inside the assistant message content block, turning:
```json
{"type": "thinking", "thinking": "The user asks about 2+2. The answer is 4."}
```
into:
```json
{"type": "thinking"}
```

Anthropic then rejects this with:
```
messages.X.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking
```

## Impact

This breaks **fallback routing** in production. When a primary model fails and LiteLLM falls back to a model with `additional_drop_params: ["thinking"]`, the conversation history (which may contain thinking blocks from prior reasoning model responses) gets corrupted, causing the fallback to also fail.

Error observed:
```
Error doing the fallback: {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error",
"message":"messages.27.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking"}}
```

## Environment

- LiteLLM version: v1.93.2
- Deployment: LiteLLM Proxy (Docker/K8s)
- Provider: Anthropic (claude-opus-5)
- Router with fallbacks enabled

## Suggested Fix

`additional_drop_params` should only strip keys from the **top-level request body** (the kwargs dict passed to the completion call), not recurse into nested structures like `messages[].content[]`. The stripping logic should be scoped to:

```python
# Only strip from top-level params
for param in additional_drop_params:
    kwargs.pop(param, None)
```

And should NOT traverse into:
- `messages[].content[]` (message content blocks)
- `messages[].tool_calls[]` (tool call arguments)
- Any other nested message payload structures

## Workaround

Remove `"thinking"` from `additional_drop_params` on models that are used as fallback targets. This means clients sending the unsupported `thinking` parameter will get a raw provider error, but fallback routing won't break.

gold.rationale:
The feature (additional_drop_params) is documented/intended to strip top-level request parameters, but the implementation recursively strips matching keys from nested structures like message content blocks, corrupting valid conversation history (e.g., Anthropic thinking blocks). This is a clear deviation from expected/documented behavior causing production failures during fallback routing, so it's a bug. It affects a widely-used provider (Anthropic) and the shared message-processing path used across providers/fallbacks, breaking production systems for users relying on additional_drop_params with fallback models - a core path issue. A workaround exists (remove the param from drop list) but that reduces functionality and reintroduces the original error, so impact remains significant. Given it affects fallback routing broadly and has a workaround, this fits P1 (major, widely-used path broken, painful workaround) - workaround exists so lower one level from P1->... wait: base severity: affects a widely-used provider (Anthropic) and shared core path (message processing) -> raise one level modifier applies for many providers/core path affected. Base is P1 already for widely-used provider broken. Workaround exists -> lower one level to P2. But shared core path affected -> raise one level back to P1. Given the ambiguity, I'll settle at P1 due to broken fallback routing in production for widely used provider/core path, workaround is only partial (loses functionality).
This is a clear, reproducible bug with a specific reproduction case and suggested fix, so it can be routed to the owning module (parameter handling / message transformation) without further clarification from a maintainer, but given it's P1, judgement/confirmation is needed per rules (any P1 requires human judgement).

items.title: [Feature]: Support OpenAI's new "ultrafast" service_tier in cost calculation
items.body:
### The Feature

OpenAI recently launched a new `service_tier` value, `"ultrafast"`, for the Responses/Chat Completions APIs (currently limited/invite-only preview, announced 2026-08-13, Cerebras-hardware-backed, exclusive to `gpt-5.6-sol`). See https://openai.com/index/previewing-ultrafast/

Requests already pass through litellm today since `service_tier` is typed as a plain string (not a `Literal`), and `_map_openai_params` only checks the param *name* is in the allowlist, not its value. However, **cost calculation silently falls back to standard/default pricing** for any `service_tier` not in `ServiceTier` (currently only `FLEX` and `PRIORITY` — see `litellm/types/utils.py`, `class ServiceTier(Enum)`), via `_get_service_tier_cost_key` in `litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py`:

```python
def _get_service_tier_cost_key(base_key: str, service_tier: Optional[str]) -> str:
    if service_tier is None:
        return base_key
    if service_tier.lower() in [ServiceTier.FLEX.value, ServiceTier.PRIORITY.value]:
        return f"{base_key}_{service_tier.lower()}"
    return base_key
```

This is the same class of silent-undercounting bug as #37046 (priority billed at default rate for gpt-4o/4.1).

### Motivation, pitch

Without native support, any deployment that enables `service_tier="ultrafast"` will log costs at the standard rate while the provider bills at the (much higher) ultrafast rate — a silent cost-tracking gap with no warning or error. We're hitting this now since OpenAI has published sticker pricing that is roughly 10x standard for this tier, and we want accurate cost attribution before enabling it for our users.

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This is a request to add support for a new, currently invite-only/limited-preview OpenAI service_tier value in cost calculation. It is a well-specified feature request (analogous to a prior fixed issue #37046) rather than an existing documented behavior being violated, since "ultrafast" is brand new and not yet part of the supported ServiceTier enum. It's a single requester describing a niche, preview-only, single-model (gpt-5.6-sol) feature with no corroborating demand from others or maintainer signal—though it does affect cost accuracy, the feature itself doesn't exist yet, making it a feature request rather than a bug. Per rules, feature requests default to P3 unless there's evidenced demand (multiple askers, maintainer intent, or widespread provider/core impact). Here it's limited to an invite-only preview tier for one specific model, so it stays P3. It is a well-specified feature request that can be routed without maintainer conversation - the fix pattern is clear (add ULTRAFAST to ServiceTier enum and cost key mapping), similar to a previously fixed analogous issue.

items.title: [Bug]: Responses bridge returns one choice per output message item — internal reasoning/plan text becomes choices[0] on n=1 chat requests (gpt-5.4+)
items.body:
### What happened?

When a `/chat/completions` request is transparently bridged to the Responses API, `_convert_response_output_to_choices()` (in `litellm/completion_extras/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py`) emits **one `choices[]` entry per Responses output `message` item**, with incrementing index. GPT-5.4+ with reasoning active frequently emits a short plan/preamble `message` item before the final answer `message` item, so an `n=1` chat request comes back with **two choices**:

- `choices[0]` = the model's internal plan/preamble text, `finish_reason: "stop"`
- `choices[1]` = the actual user-facing answer

Virtually every Chat Completions client (OpenAI SDKs, LangChain/LangGraph, ...) reads `choices[0]` only, so **the user is shown the model's internal reasoning and the real answer is silently discarded**. The caller never asked for `n>1`, and nothing in the response signals that choices[0] is not the answer.

This is easy to hit unknowingly: gpt-5.4+ rejects function tools on `/v1/chat/completions` whenever reasoning is active, and `responses_api_bridge_check()` (litellm/main.py) reroutes those requests through the Responses API automatically. So a caller who sets `reasoning_effort: "low"` on a chat request with tools gets opted into the bridge — and into this bug — without changing anything else.

**Observed in production** (2026-08-17, LiteLLM proxy in front of `openai/gpt-5.4`, `reasoning_effort: "low"`, 15 function tools, non-streaming): a customer-facing agent replied to an end user with:

> "Need ask for specific date because resolver failed, but can mention 2-bed offered. Must start exact greeting Hello! I'm ELI... despite additionalInstruction conflict due explicit. ..."

while the real answer sat unread in `choices[1]`.

We also hit the sibling shape `[message item, function_call item]` → `[text choice, tool_calls choice]`, where reading choices[0] makes an agent framework treat the turn as final and **skip the tool call entirely**. That shape is already covered by PR #33931 — but #33931 explicitly does *not* merge multiple plain `message` items (its multi-message handling still emits one choice per message), so this issue remains after it merges.

### Expected behavior

For a request with `n` absent or `n=1`, the bridge should return **exactly one choice**, like the native Chat Completions endpoint does:

- the final `message` item's text is `choices[0].message.content`
- earlier `message` items (preamble/plan) belong in `message.reasoning_content` (alongside text from `reasoning` items), not in a separate choice
- if the turn contains tool calls, they live on that same single choice with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"` (PR #33931's merge)

`choices[]` cardinality should be driven by the caller's `n`, never by the provider's output item count.

### Repro

Any gpt-5.4+ chat completion that (a) gets bridged to the Responses API and (b) returns `[reasoning?, message, message]` output items. Minimal unit-level repro against the transform:

```python
from openai.types.responses import ResponseOutputMessage, ResponseOutputText
from litellm.completion_extras.litellm_responses_transformation.transformation import (
    LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler,
)

items = [
    ResponseOutputMessage(
        id="msg_1", role="assistant", status="completed", type="message",
        content=[ResponseOutputText(type="output_text", text="Internal plan: ask for the date first.", annotations=[])],
    ),
    ResponseOutputMessage(
        id="msg_2", role="assistant", status="completed", type="message",
        content=[ResponseOutputText(type="output_text", text="Hello! What move-in date works for you?", annotations=[])],
    ),
]

choices = LiteLLMResponsesTransformationHandler._convert_response_output_to_choices(items)
assert len(choices) == 1, f"expected 1 choice for an n=1 request, got {len(choices)}"
# fails: len(choices) == 2, choices[0] is the internal plan
```

### Related

- PR #33931 — merges message + tool_calls into one choice; does **not** cover the multiple-plain-messages case.
- PR #33242 / issue #33221 — the auto-bridge trigger (function tools + reasoning on gpt-5.4+).

### Relevant log output

```
POST /v1/chat/completions, model=gpt-5.4, reasoning_effort=low, 15 function tools, n not set
-> response: 2 choices, finish_reasons ["stop","stop"]
choices[0].message.content = "Need ask for specific date because resolver failed, ..."   # internal plan
choices[1].message.content = "Hello! I'm ELI, the virtual leasing agent for ..."         # real answer, discarded by clients
```

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

Yes

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

Reproduced on main (2026-08-18) via code inspection of `_convert_response_output_to_choices`; observed in prod behind `main-stable`.

gold.rationale: This is a clear bug: the Responses-to-Chat-Completions bridge violates the documented/expected contract that an n=1 chat completion request returns exactly one choice. Instead it emits one choice per output message item, causing internal reasoning/plan text to be surfaced as choices[0] while discarding the real answer, or causing tool calls to be skipped entirely. This is not a docs issue (code violates the expected API contract), not a feature request (existing functionality is broken), and not a security issue in the traditional sense, though it does cause silent data corruption/loss of the actual answer for end users. It affects a widely-used provider path (OpenAI gpt-5.4+ auto-bridged whenever reasoning + tools are used on /chat/completions), which is an increasingly common configuration for agentic workflows (LangChain/LangGraph clients), and there's no caller-side workaround since it's triggered automatically by responses_api_bridge_check() without any config change. It also silently causes agent frameworks to skip tool calls or expose internal reasoning to end users — a functional/production-impacting bug, not cosmetic. Given many callers use OpenAI gpt-5.4+ with reasoning_effort and tools, and this is automatically triggered without opt-in, impact is broad across users hitting this code path (shared core bridging logic), though it's specific to one reasoning-capable model family and requires an automatic bridge trigger, so not "most users" broadly. A repro is given, is well-specified and confirmed in code inspection, with production evidence. There is no caller-facing workaround (since the bridging is automatic), but partial mitigation could be avoiding reasoning_effort + tools together, which is a stated modifier that could lower severity — however, this would break existing use cases. Given a widely-used provider (OpenAI) and shared core code path (Responses bridge) is affected and this can silently corrupt agent responses/break tool calling (already partially fixed by PR #33931 for the sibling case), I'll set urgency to P1: a major, widely used provider (OpenAI/gpt-5.4) integration is broken for common reasoning+tools usage without an easy workaround. Since this is P1, per rules this requires needs_human=true (judgement/reproduction confirmation, and it touches core bridging logic affecting many downstream integrations).

items.title: [Bug]: Compression/caching savings always $0.00 for any custom (non-cost-map) model, even with a single deployment
items.body:
# [Bug]: Compression/caching savings always $0.00 for any custom (non-cost-map) model, even with a single deployment

## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

Related: #37117 (same root cause in `savings.py`, but scoped there to *multiple deployments per `model_name` + `cost-based-routing`*). Filing separately because the trigger is much broader — a **single deployment with default routing** is enough — and because there is an additional key-shadowing behaviour that constrains the fix. Also related: #35693 (same `shared_backend_model_info()` stripping, surfaced as an unsuppressible cache-cost warning).

## What happened?

The Cost Optimization dashboard reports **"$0.00" next to a perfectly correct non-zero "N tokens compressed"**. In our case: `2,642,007 tokens compressed`, `compression_savings_spend = $0.00`, while real `spend` for the same rollup row was `$11.71`.

The trigger is not multi-deployment routing. It is simply:

> the deployment carries operator-supplied custom pricing **and** the model is not in LiteLLM's built-in cost map — i.e. **any self-hosted / custom model**.

Chain of events for a single deployment:

1. `Router._create_deployment()` registers the deployment's pricing under **two** keys:
   - the deployment UUID -> full pricing retained
   - `{provider}/{model}` -> passed through `shared_backend_model_info()`, which **strips every pricing field**
2. The **public `model_name`** — the value the spend log records, and therefore the only thing `compute_savings_spend()` receives — is **never registered with pricing at all**.
3. `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` calls `litellm.get_model_info(model=<public name>, custom_llm_provider=...)`, which raises `"This model isn't mapped yet"` for a custom model.
4. That raise is caught and the helper "falls open" to `(0.0, 0.0)`.
5. `compression = saved_tokens * 0.0 == 0.0`.

Billing (`spend`) is unaffected, because response-cost calculation reads the deployment object directly instead of going through `litellm.model_cost`. Only the savings columns break, which is why the token count and the dollar figure disagree.

## Relevant log output

```
get_model_info('muse-glimmer-30b','openai')
  -> Exception: This model isn't mapped yet. model=muse-glimmer-30b, custom_llm_provider=openai

_input_and_cache_read_cost('muse-glimmer-30b','openai') = (0.0, 0.0)
```

DB rollup row (`LiteLLM_DailyUserSpend`) showing the contradiction:

```
date=2026-08-18 model=muse-glimmer-30b custom_llm_provider=openai
  prompt_tokens             = 31,274,060
  spend                     = 11.7122      <-- billing works
  compression_saved_tokens  =  2,642,007   <-- correct
  compression_savings_spend =  0.0         <-- should be ~$0.9247
  api_requests              =  2,287
```

The per-request guardrail metadata is recorded correctly, so nothing is wrong upstream of pricing:

```json
{"guardrail_name": "headroom-compression", "guardrail_provider": "headroom",
 "guardrail_status": "success",
 "guardrail_response": {"tokens_before": 49323, "tokens_after": 49206, "tokens_saved": 117}}
```

## Steps to Reproduce

Minimal config — **one** deployment, no `router_settings`, no `cost-based-routing`:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: muse-glimmer-30b
    litellm_params:
      model: muse-glimmer-30b
      custom_llm_provider: openai
      api_base: https://your-self-hosted-endpoint/v1
      api_key: os.environ/MY_TOKEN
      input_cost_per_token: 3.5e-07
      output_cost_per_token: 1.5e-06

guardrails:
  - guardrail_name: headroom-compression
    litellm_params:
      guardrail: headroom
      mode: pre_call
      api_base: http://headroom-proxy:8787
      default_on: true
```

Send traffic through it, then read `/user/daily/activity` (or the Cost Optimization tile): `total_compression_saved_tokens` climbs, `total_compression_savings_spend` stays `0.0`.

Reproduced directly in the running container, replaying what `Router` does for that single deployment:

```python
import litellm
from litellm.router import shared_backend_model_info
from litellm.proxy.spend_tracking.savings import _input_and_cache_read_cost

PRICE = {"input_cost_per_token": 3.5e-07, "output_cost_per_token": 1.5e-06,
         "cache_read_input_token_cost": 3.5e-07}

full = dict(PRICE, id="dep-solo")
litellm.register_model(model_cost={"dep-solo": full})
litellm.register_model(model_cost={"openai/solo-model": shared_backend_model_info(full)})

print(litellm.model_cost["dep-solo"]["input_cost_per_token"])          # 3.5e-07
print(litellm.model_cost["openai/solo-model"]["input_cost_per_token"]) # None
print(litellm.model_cost.get("solo-model"))                           # None
print(_input_and_cache_read_cost("solo-model", "openai"))              # (0.0, 0.0)
```

Output:

```
model_cost['dep-solo'].input           = 3.5e-07
model_cost['openai/solo-model'].input  = None
model_cost['solo-model']               = None
LOOKUP('solo-model','openai')          = (0.0, 0.0)
```

### Second finding: the provider-prefixed key shadows the public name

Important for whichever fix is chosen. `get_model_info()` prefers the combined `{provider}/{model}` key, and `Router` has already created that key *without* pricing. So registering pricing under the bare public name is **not** sufficient:

```
after pricing bare 'solo-model':
  model_cost['solo-model'].input        = 3.5e-07
  model_cost['openai/solo-model'].input = None
  LOOKUP('solo-model','openai')         = (0.0, 0.0)   <-- STILL ZERO

after also pricing 'openai/solo-model':
  LOOKUP('solo-model','openai')         = (3.5e-07, 3.5e-07)   <-- fixed
```

## What did you expect to happen?

`compression_savings_spend` / `prompt_caching_savings_spend` should price saved tokens at the deployment's configured input rate whenever that rate is known — which it demonstrably is, since ordinary `spend` is calculated correctly from the same deployment. Expected for the row above: `2,642,007 x 3.5e-07 = $0.9247`.

At minimum, savings should never silently render `$0.00` beside a non-zero token count; that reads as "compression achieved nothing" rather than "pricing lookup failed".

## Suggested fix

Preferred: make the savings path deployment-aware rather than name-aware, so key shadowing is irrelevant.

**Option C** (in addition to Options A/B in #37117): have `_input_and_cache_read_cost()` consult `Router.get_deployment_model_info(model_id, model)` before falling back to `get_model_info()`. `savings.py` already imports `Router` for the autorouter baseline and `_effective_model_info()` already performs deployment-aware resolution, so most of the plumbing exists.

Two smaller points regardless of approach:

1. Any cost-map-repair fix must also write the `{provider}/{model}` key, or stop `shared_backend_model_info()` from stripping pricing when a single deployment owns that key (cf. #35693).
2. Consider distinguishing "priced at zero" from "price unknown". The current fall-open to `(0.0, 0.0)` turns a lookup failure into a confident `$0.00`; a debug log exists but nothing surfaces to the operator.

`compression_savings_spend` is written with `increment`, so historical rows will remain `$0.00` after a fix and need a separate backfill.

## Workaround

A `CustomLogger` registered via `litellm_settings.callbacks` that mirrors each deployment's pricing (read back from `litellm.model_cost[<deployment id>]`) onto both the public `model_name` and the `{provider}/{model}` key, re-synced on an interval to catch DB/UI-added deployments. It invents no prices: deployments without custom pricing are skipped, so nothing is over-reported.

Verified end-to-end against the live proxy after deploying it:

```
delta saved_tokens = 734
delta saved_usd    = 0.000256900
expected (734 x 3.5e-07) = 0.000256900   MATCH

/user/daily/activity -> total_compression_savings_spend = 0.00113715   (was 0.0)
```

Also confirmed to survive a pod restart (860 saved tokens -> $0.000301, exact match).

## Are you a ML Ops Team?

Yes

## What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.96.2 (also verified present in v1.97.0)

## Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This is a clear, well-reproduced bug: compression/caching savings computation falls back to (0.0, 0.0) for any custom model with operator-supplied pricing not in litellm's built-in cost map, because the pricing lookup key used by savings.py doesn't align with how Router registers custom pricing (shared_backend_model_info strips pricing, and provider-prefixed key shadows bare name). Billing/spend works correctly, but the savings/cost-optimization dashboard reports incorrect ($0.00) values despite correct token counts — this is "incorrect cost accounting" per the bug rules. It's not a docs issue (code violates intended behavior) nor a feature request (existing behavior is broken) nor a security issue. This affects any self-hosted/custom model user relying on the compression/caching savings dashboard — a fairly broad audience for self-hosted deployments, but it's a narrower reporting/analytics feature (not core request/response path), and a workaround isn't really available besides not trusting the dashboard. Given it's scoped to a specific dashboard metric (not blocking core requests or billing), and affects a subset of users (those using custom models + compression guardrails), P2 fits best. It's well-documented with clear reproduction steps and root cause analysis, so a maintainer doesn't need to triage from scratch, but the fix requires resolving the key-shadowing constraint (a judgement call on how to fix registration/lookup), so some human judgement is warranted before implementation, though the issue reporter already suggests both a root cause and a working fix pattern. Given the clarity of repro and root cause, this could be routed directly to the owning module (savings.py) without discussion.

items.title: Add Skills page to Internal Users page visibility settings
items.body:
### Problem

In the LiteLLM Admin UI, under **Admin Settings -> UI Settings**, admins can choose which pages an internal user can see (e.g., Models, Teams, Keys, Spend, etc.).

However, the **Skills** page is missing from this list, so there is no way to hide it from internal users without disabling the entire Admin UI (`DISABLE_ADMIN_UI=true`) or removing the Anthropic provider configuration.

### Context

- The **Skills** page is visible in the Admin UI, but there is no per-role/per-user visibility toggle in **Admin Settings -> UI Settings**.
- For teams that do not want end users to access the Skills page, the only documented way to hide it is to disable the whole Admin UI.

### Request

Add a **Skills** visibility toggle in **Admin Settings -> UI Settings**, so admins can show or hide the Skills page per user/role, just like the other UI sections.

### Possible implementation

Expose a `ui_page_visible.skills` flag (or equivalent) in the UI visibility configuration and respect it when rendering the sidebar/routes.

### Alternatives considered

- `DISABLE_ADMIN_UI=true`: disables the entire UI, not acceptable.

### Environment

- LiteLLM version: latest stable
- Deployment: self-hosted proxy with Admin UI

gold.rationale: This is a request for new functionality: adding a per-user visibility toggle for the Skills page in the UI settings, which doesn't currently exist. This is a well-specified feature request with a clear implementation suggestion, but comes from a single requester with no corroborating demand from others. It's a narrow UI settings addition, not affecting a widely-used core path broadly, so it defaults to P3. It's well-specified enough to be routed without further discussion.

items.title: [Feature]: Bump Granian from 2.7.4 to 2.8.1 in the published proxy
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.
