There is no open or closed issue/PR for Granian 2.8.x. The last Granian bump was Dependabot [#28538](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/28538) (`2.5.7` → `2.7.4`, closed unmerged) and the security bundle [#29208](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29208) that landed `2.7.4`.

### The Feature

Please evaluate and bump the Granian version shipped with the official proxy images / PyPI package from **2.7.4 to 2.8.1**.

`pyproject.toml` already allows `granian>=2.7.4,<3.0`, so 2.8.1 is in range. The published lock and images still ship **2.7.4**.

Granian **2.8.1** was released 2026-08-05 ([release](https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian/releases/tag/v2.8.1)). OSV reports no CVEs on 2.7.4 or 2.8.1 — this is not a security fire drill. The last LiteLLM Granian bump *was* CVE-driven (`CVE-2026-42544` / `CVE-2026-42545` in #29208), which is why I am asking here instead of sending a lockfile-only PR.

**Please review Granian 2.8.0 breaking changes before bumping** ([2.8.0 notes](https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian/releases/tag/v2.8.0)):

- Linux multi-worker + respawn now requires kernel ≥ 5.14 **and** `net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` enabled.
- Non-configurable backpressure on streamed / iterable ASGI responses (can change `/v1/chat/completions` streaming memory vs throughput).
- Worker loop / shutdown refactors (relevant if `--max_requests_before_restart` is in use).
- WSGI environ priority change (should not affect the ASGI proxy path).

2.8.1 itself is a patch on top of that: ASGI websocket performance regression fix, `PyFutureAwaitable` interface fix, RSGI websocket close, relaxed atomics.

I can send a lockfile PR if you want the bump after this review.

### User Flow

Before this feature (today): an operator who starts the official proxy with Granian gets 2.7.4 and cannot pick up the 2.8.1 server without rebuilding the image themselves.

1. They deploy `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:1.97.0` (or `pip install litellm==1.97.0`) and start the proxy with `--run_granian` plus TLS.
2. They send `GET https://<litellm-host>/health/liveliness` with HTTP/2. It returns `HTTP/2 200`, `server: granian`, body `"I'm alive!"`.
3. The same URL over HTTP/1.1 also returns `200` and `server: granian`.
4. They have no supported way to run Granian 2.8.1 on that official image. Workaround is a custom image / fork of the lockfile.

After this feature (ideal user flow): the same official image ships Granian 2.8.1 after the 2.8.0 behavior is reviewed.

1. They deploy the next official image / PyPI release and start the proxy with the same `--run_granian` plus TLS.
2. They send the same `GET https://<litellm-host>/health/liveliness` with HTTP/2. It still returns `HTTP/2 200`, `server: granian`, body `"I'm alive!"`.
3. The same URL over HTTP/1.1 still returns `200` and `server: granian`.
4. Streamed `POST https://<litellm-host>/v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true` still completes with SSE `data:` chunks and a normal `[DONE]` (this is the 2.8.0 backpressure check).
5. If they use worker respawn (`--max_requests_before_restart`), workers still recycle without dropping the listener.

### How far you got

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

- Image: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:1.97.0`
- Started with `--run_granian` and in-guest TLS
- Public host: `https://llm.kubetee.ai`

Version or commit:

- LiteLLM `1.97.0` (`stable/1.97.x`)
- Granian inside that image: `2.7.4`
- Constraint already in tree: `granian>=2.7.4,<3.0`

Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends:

```
$ curl -sS -D - --http2 --max-time 15 https://llm.kubetee.ai/health/liveliness
HTTP/2 200
content-length: 12
content-type: application/json
x-frame-options: DENY
content-security-policy: frame-ancestors 'none'
x-content-type-options: nosniff
server: granian
date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 22:24:58 GMT

"I'm alive!"
```

```
$ curl -sS -D - --http1.1 --max-time 15 https://llm.kubetee.ai/health/liveliness
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-length: 12
content-type: application/json
x-frame-options: DENY
content-security-policy: frame-ancestors 'none'
x-content-type-options: nosniff
server: granian
date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 22:25:00 GMT

"I'm alive!"
```

What stopped me there:

HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 both work on 2.7.4. The missing piece is only the official 2.8.1 bump. I did not open a lockfile PR because 2.8.0 has breaking changes that need a maintainer look (streaming backpressure + Linux `tcp_migrate_req` / multi-worker respawn), and because `.github/dependabot.yaml` currently watches GitHub Actions only, so Dependabot will not open this.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users?

No

gold.rationale: This is a request to bump a dependency (Granian) to a newer version, which is a new behavior/feature request rather than fixing broken behavior - the current version works fine as shown by the tests. There's no evidenced demand from multiple users, just a single well-researched requester. No security issue since OSV reports no CVEs. Per rules, feature requests default to P3 unless there's evidenced demand (multiple askers, maintainer intent, or widely-used provider/core path affected) - this is a single detailed requester. It does require product-direction judgement since 2.8.0 has breaking changes (multi-worker respawn requirements, streaming backpressure changes) that need maintainer evaluation before deciding to bump, making this a judgement call rather than a simple routing decision.

items.title: [Bug]: Batch spend is permanently lost when a client status poll records the terminal state before the batch cost job's next cycle
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

Closest neighbors, neither a duplicate: #37156 covers the cost poller retiring terminal batches unbilled when the poller itself sees the terminal transition (fixed by #37205), and #37153 covered the stale sweep's handling of completed unprocessed rows. This issue is the remaining ordering: the client sees the terminal transition first

### What happened?

When a client polls GET /v1/batches/{batch_id} through the proxy while waiting for a cancelled or failed batch to finalize, the proxy records the provider's terminal status the moment the client sees it. The background batch cost job skips batches already recorded as cancelled or failed, so it never revisits that batch and the spend for its completed requests is never written

PR #37205 makes the cost job bill any terminal batch with an output file, but only when the job notices the terminal transition itself. A polling client (the normal OpenAI SDK pattern) checks every few seconds while the job's default interval is one hour, so the client effectively always stamps the terminal status first and the spend is still lost. In the reproduction below the job's last look at the batch was 9 seconds before the provider finalized; the client's next poll landed first, and nine subsequent job cycles plus a full proxy restart never billed the 86 completed requests

Expected: the completed portion of a cancelled or failed batch is billed regardless of whether the client or the background job sees the terminal status first

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer cancels an in-progress batch and polls it through the gateway until it finalizes; the gateway serves the partial results but never records any spend for them

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing
4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds, the way the OpenAI SDK polling helpers do; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and request_counts.completed 86
5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with 86 result lines carrying real token usage
6. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} shows only the $0 batch-creation row and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows spend 0.0, permanently: hours of cost-job cycles and even a gateway restart never bill it

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same polled batch is billed for its completed work within one cost-job cycle

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider
3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing
4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and non-zero request_counts.completed
5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with the completed result lines
6. Within one cost-job cycle GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} gains a batch-retrieval row with the real cost and token counts of those completed requests, and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the matching non-zero spend

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini-batch
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
    model_info:
      mode: batch
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

Env: `LITELLM_LICENSE` set (the batch cost job is enterprise), `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=120` (short enough to observe many job cycles; the default 3600 makes the race even more certain), fresh Postgres DB

Version or commit: `b34cbb18e2` (the tip of PR #37205's branch, so the #37156 fix is already included; the base branch without #37205 loses the spend on every ordering, not just this one)

Commands and their full output (key redacted; live proxy on localhost:49726, real OpenAI batch API):

1. Create a key with a user_id, upload a 2000-request JSONL, create the batch:
   ```bash
   KEY=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"lit5663-clobber","user_id":"lit5663-user","models":["gpt-5.4-mini-batch"]}' | jq -r .key)
   FILE=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -F purpose=batch -F 'target_model_names=gpt-5.4-mini-batch' -F file=@cancelleg2.jsonl | jq -r .id)
   BATCH=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"input_file_id\":\"$FILE\",\"endpoint\":\"/v1/chat/completions\",\"completion_window\":\"24h\"}" | jq -r .id)
   ```
2. Poll `GET /v1/batches/$BATCH` through the proxy every 2-3 s (the SDK pattern). At the first in_progress poll with completed 32, cancel through the proxy: `curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:49726/v1/batches/$BATCH/cancel" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` returns HTTP 200 with status cancelling
3. Keep polling; ~25 min later (provider batch_6a836d8e1c30819090dd7133000d6a6f, cancelled_at 14:08:31 PDT) the first cancelled poll shows `"status": "cancelled"`, a populated output_file_id, `"request_counts": {"total": 2000, "completed": 86, "failed": 0}`
4. `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` returns HTTP 200 with 86 JSONL result lines totaling 1634 prompt + 344 completion = 1978 tokens of real completed work
5. Across six cost-job cycles: `curl -s "http://localhost:49726/spend/logs?request_id=$BATCH" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER"` shows only the $0 `acreate_batch` row, `spend/logs?request_id=${BATCH}_batch_cost` returns `[]`, and `/key/info` reports `"spend": 0.0`
6. Restarting the proxy on the same DB and waiting three more cycles changes nothing: still no `aretrieve_batch` row, key spend still 0.0. The exclusion is durable state, not a warm-cache artifact

Timing detail from the proxy log: the cost job examined this batch on every one of its 22 cycles while the batch was non-terminal (last at 14:08:25), the client's poll recorded cancelling -> cancelled at 14:08:34, and none of the nine subsequent cycles examined the batch again

### What a fix PR should look like

Two workable shapes, either is fine:

- Include provider-terminal statuses in the cost job's pickup so a row stamped cancelled/failed with an output file and not yet billed still gets billed once. This needs an upgrade guard (for example a created_at cutoff) so pre-existing terminal rows from before the fix do not get retroactively billed as one spike on deploy, and it should mind the poll-page slots (MAX_OBJECTS_PER_POLL_CYCLE) so old rows cannot starve new ones
- Alternatively, keep the retrieve/cancel path from stamping a terminal status onto a not-yet-billed row (stamp it only once spend has been written, letting the cost job see the transition itself)

The regression test belongs in tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py: simulate the retrieve-first ordering (row already carrying the provider's terminal status, batch_processed false, output file present) and assert the job still bills it exactly once

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

litellm_internal_staging @ f04b1dad plus PR #37205 (b34cbb18e2)

gold.rationale: This is a clear regression/bug: batch spend for completed requests is permanently lost when a client's status poll records the terminal state before the background cost job's next cycle, effectively negating the fix from PR #37205 for the common client-polling pattern. It affects the shared batch billing core path (any provider using batch mode), causing silent, permanent revenue loss with no workaround (job restarts and many cycles don't recover it). This is a widely-affecting core billing bug, related to a recent fix that didn't fully resolve the issue (regression-adjacent), so it should be raised in urgency. No workaround exists, and it affects the shared spend-tracking core path, so P1 (not P0 since it's not a security issue or totally broken system, but a significant billing correctness issue affecting many users of batch API across providers). Needs human review because it requires judgment on how to correctly synchronize state between the client-polling path and the cost job, and confirming the exact reproduction and fix approach - it's also P1 which mandates human review per rules.

items.title: No renewal path when an upstream grant has neither expires_in nor refresh_token
items.body:
## Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

## The Feature

When an upstream token response carries neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`:

- the access envelope gets `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` (3600), since
  `_envelope_ttl_seconds(None)` returns the cap, and
- no refresh envelope is minted, because `discoverable_endpoints.py` skips that
  step when the response has no `refresh_token`.

The result is that the client has no renewal path at all. Recovery is a full
interactive `authorization_code` flow, roughly every hour, for the lifetime of
the integration.

Some providers issue access tokens that do not expire, and signal that by omitting
`expires_in`. Nothing on the wire distinguishes this from "expires, lifetime
unstated", so the gateway assumes the latter. We are not asking it to assume
otherwise. The problem is what happens next: for this shape of grant there is no
bounded renewal mechanism, only re-authorization.

Two mechanisms already exist and neither reaches this case.

**The upstream 401 relay.** For `is_oauth_delegate` servers,
`mcp_server_manager` relays an upstream 401 as `MCPUpstreamAuthError` so callers
turn it into a 401 with the upstream's own `WWW-Authenticate` and re-run the OAuth
flow. The comment states the intent: only a 401 is a re-auth signal, and it is the
caller's to resolve. That is the right design, but the access envelope's own `exp`
fires first, so the upstream is never asked and the relay never runs. The gateway's
locally chosen expiry pre-empts the provider's own answer.

**The refresh envelope.** #32980 added refresh envelopes and scoped them to grants
returning a `refresh_token`:

> A new refresh envelope is re-issued only when the upstream returns a new refresh token, so the design mirrors the upstream authorization server's own rotation policy rather than reinventing it: against a rotating upstream the client rotates and the upstream detects reuse of a retired token; against a non-rotating upstream the original refresh envelope stands until its bounded TTL.

That covers a non-rotating upstream, which keeps its refresh envelope for the
14-day bound. It does not cover an upstream that returns no refresh token at all,
which gets no envelope and therefore no bound other than the 1h access cap.

We are not asking for the access cap to be raised or removed. The constant's own
docstring anticipates that argument and rejects it:

> Hard ceiling on ACCESS envelope lifetime [...] matching the 1h lifetime of the
> BYOK session bearer this module's signing approach is borrowed from: a client-held
> credential should never outlive a bounded window even when the upstream token does.

We think that is correct. The cap does not bound the provider's token, it bounds
the client-held bearer, and its value is that a leaked envelope dies on its own
without requiring the principal's access to be revoked wholesale. "The provider
says the token does not expire" is not an answer to envelope theft. Nor would
dropping the expiry work mechanically, since `exp` is a required claim on open.

Give this grant shape the same treatment the 14-day refresh bound already
represents: when the upstream returns neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`,
mint a refresh envelope sealing the access token, and let the `refresh_token`
grant re-mint a fresh 1h access envelope from the sealed grant.

This seems to fit the reasoning already documented on
`MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS`:

> A refresh envelope only renews the short-lived access envelope, and each renewal re-validates the sealed litellm key (revocation gates it) and is re-minted with a fresh window, so the practical bound is idle time, not a fixed session.

Both properties hold here. The credential is presented only back to the token
endpoint rather than held as a bearer for upstream calls, and each renewal
re-validates the sealed identity. The 1h client-held access cap is untouched,
revocation still gates every renewal, and hourly interactive re-authorization
becomes a 14-day idle bound.

One honest caveat: the current refresh path unwraps the sealed refresh token and
POSTs `grant_type=refresh_token` upstream, so this needs a distinct arm that
re-mints from the sealed grant without an upstream call, not a straight reuse of
the existing flow.

A per-server override for the access cap would also solve our immediate problem
and is a smaller change, since `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is read only by
`envelope.py` and has no config field or environment variable today. We suggest it
second because it needs an operator to declare provider behavior correctly, and
because it weakens the client-held-bearer bound that the docstring above is
protecting. If you did prefer this shape, `MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is a
same-shaped sibling that an override should probably cover too.

Happy to send a PR for either direction.

## User Flow

Before this feature (today):

- Someone authorizes an MCP server once through the gateway and starts working.
- Roughly an hour later the credential is gone. There is no renewal path, so the
  only way back is the full interactive authorization flow.
- That repeats every hour, for as long as they use the integration.

After this feature:

- Someone authorizes once. Renewal happens against the token endpoint without
  their involvement.
- Interactive re-authorization is needed only after a long idle period, bounded by
  the existing 14-day refresh window, rather than hourly.

## How far you got

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  example_server:
    url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp
    transport: http
    auth_type: oauth_delegate
    dcr_bridge: true
```

Version or commit:

1.97.0

Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends:

Complete the DCR flow against the server above, against an upstream whose token
response includes neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`. The token response
returns an access envelope and no `refresh_token` field. There is no further
command to run: no refresh grant exists to renew with, so the flow dead-ends at
re-authorization once the access envelope reaches its `exp`.

What stopped me there:

The client has no renewal path and must repeat the interactive `authorization_code` flow roughly every hour.

## What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

## LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users?

No

gold.rationale: This is a well-documented architectural gap in the OAuth delegate/MCP server integration: when an upstream token grant has neither expires_in nor refresh_token, the gateway has no renewal path other than hourly full re-authorization, because the access envelope hits the 1h cap and no refresh envelope is minted. The code behaves as documented/intended (the cap and refresh scoping are deliberate design choices), but the combination leaves a real gap in expected behavior for a class of legitimate upstream providers - this is closer to a missing capability (feature) than a defect in existing documented behavior, since it requires new logic (a new refresh-envelope-minting arm and a distinct re-mint-without-upstream-call path) rather than fixing something that contradicts current docs. The reporter frames it as "The Feature" and offers two possible implementation directions, explicitly asking for maintainer input on which direction to take. This requires product-direction judgement from a maintainer (which of two designs to adopt, or whether to build this at all), so needs_human=true. Given it affects any provider issuing non-expiring tokens without refresh tokens (a plausible but not necessarily majority pattern), and there's a stated workaround (re-authenticate hourly, painful but functional) plus no corroborating evidence of multiple users hitting this rather than a single detailed reporter, this fits P2 at most for a feature with a single detailed requester — per the rules a single requester, however detailed, defaults to P3. There's a workaround (repeat interactive auth) which is painful, which per feature-request classification doesn't independently raise urgency since features default to P3 with promotion only via evidenced multi-party demand. No regression, no multi-provider breadth signal beyond one report. So urgency = P3.

items.title: [Bug]: GET /v1/batches returns 200 for ?limit=0, -1, 101 and 1000; limit=0 returns 20 records
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

`GET /v1/batches?limit=` returns HTTP 200 for values outside 1..100. On an account holding 99 batches:

| `limit` | Records returned | `has_more` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | 20 | true |
| -1 | 0 | false |
| 1 | 1 | true |
| 2 | 2 | true |
| 5 | 5 | true |
| 101 | 97 | false |
| 1000 | 97 | false |

OpenAI returns HTTP 400 for values outside 1..100:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Invalid 'limit': integer above maximum value. Expected a value <= 100, but got 101 instead.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "limit",
    "code": "integer_above_max_value"
  }
}
```

### Code as it stands at v1.94.3

`litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py:574`:

```python
async def list_batches(
    request: Request,
    fastapi_response: Response,
    provider: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: Optional[int] = None,
    after: Optional[str] = None,
    user_api_key_dict: UserAPIKeyAuth = Depends(user_api_key_auth),
    target_model_names: Optional[str] = None,
):
```

No `Query(...)` constraint is attached to `limit`.

---

### User Flow

**Before a (hypothetical) fix: a script paginating batch history computes a page size of 0 and receives 20 records**

1. The script sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=100` and processes the returned page
2. Its remaining-count arithmetic yields `0` on the final iteration
3. It sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=0`
4. The response is `200` carrying 20 records, so the script processes 20 records it did not request
5. A separate call with `?limit=101` returns `200` carrying 97 records
6. A call with `?limit=-1` returns `200` carrying 0 records

**After a (hypothetical) fix: values outside 1..100 return 400**

1. The script sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=100` and processes the returned page
2. Its remaining-count arithmetic yields `0` on the final iteration
3. It sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=0`
4. The response is `400` with `"Invalid 'limit'"` and `"param": "limit"`
5. `?limit=101` returns `400`
6. `?limit=-1` returns `400`

---

### Proof the bug occurs

**Version**: `litellm 1.94.3`, image digest `sha256:b7d979bac2a9e8fbb7d55272ef5f1f4a08ab365de8f78b1800834ca718d4c941`. The account held 99 batches. No provider call is made on this path.

**Config the proxy ran with**

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gpt-5-batch
    litellm_params:
      model: azure/gpt-5-batch-2025-08-07
      api_base: os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE
      api_key: os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

**Commands and their full output**

```
$ for L in 0 -1 1 2 5 101 1000; do
    N=$(curl -s "http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?limit=$L" \
          -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \
          | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d.get("data",[])), "has_more=",d.get("has_more"))')
    printf 'limit=%-6s -> %s\n' "$L" "$N"
  done

limit=0      -> 20 has_more= True
limit=-1     -> 0 has_more= False
limit=1      -> 1 has_more= True
limit=2      -> 2 has_more= True
limit=5      -> 5 has_more= True
limit=101    -> 97 has_more= False
limit=1000   -> 97 has_more= False
```

Status code for one of them:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' 'http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?limit=0' \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY"
HTTP 200
```

The total returned by a single in-range request:

```
$ curl -s 'http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?limit=100' -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \
    | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("total:", len(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]))'
total: 99
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.94.3

gold.rationale: The /v1/batches endpoint fails to validate the `limit` query parameter, accepting values outside the documented/expected 1..100 range and returning inconsistent, incorrect results (200 with wrong record counts) instead of a 400 error like OpenAI's API. This is a clear behavioral bug: the endpoint returns wrong output for out-of-range inputs, which could break pagination logic in client scripts. There's a clear reproduction with exact steps and version. This affects a specific endpoint (batches) rather than the shared core path, and a workaround exists (validate/clamp limit client-side before sending). It's not a security issue, not a docs issue, and not a feature request since the intended behavior (matching OpenAI's validation contract) already exists in spec but is not implemented correctly.

items.title: [Bug]: Proxy shutdown always fails with AttributeError when Redis cluster mode is enabled (async_redis_conn_pool is None)
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

With Redis **cluster mode** enabled, every proxy shutdown ends in an unhandled
`AttributeError`, and uvicorn reports `Application shutdown failed. Exiting.`

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'disconnect'
  File "litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 1232, in <lifespan>
    await proxy_shutdown_event()
  File "litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 843, in proxy_shutdown_event
    await litellm.cache.disconnect()
  File "litellm/caching/caching.py", line 913, in disconnect
    await self.cache.disconnect()
  File "litellm/caching/redis_cache.py", line 1356, in disconnect
    await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True)
```

This is deterministic, not intermittent — it fires on every shutdown.

### User Flow

### Suggested fix

Two parts:

1. Guard the base class — `redis_cache.py`:
   ```python
   async def disconnect(self):
       if self.async_redis_conn_pool is not None:
           await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True)
   ```
2. Give `RedisClusterCache` a real teardown, since the guard alone leaks the cluster client:
   ```python
   async def disconnect(self):
       if self.redis_async_redis_cluster_client is not None:
           await self.redis_async_redis_cluster_client.aclose()
       await super().disconnect()
   ```
   `aclose()` is already the primitive used in `test_connection()` in that same file.

Wrapping the `litellm.cache.disconnect()` call in `proxy_shutdown_event()` in a
try/except would also stop one cache failure from aborting the rest of shutdown, independent
of this bug.

### Proof the bug occurs

### Root cause

`get_redis_connection_pool()` returns `None` by design in cluster mode, because a
`RedisCluster` builds its own per-node pools rather than taking a shared
`BlockingConnectionPool` — `litellm/_redis.py:691-692`:

```python
if "startup_nodes" in redis_kwargs:
    return None
```

`RedisCache.__init__` stores that `None` unconditionally (`redis_cache.py:309`), and
`RedisCache.disconnect()` then dereferences it with no guard (`redis_cache.py:1355-1356`):

```python
async def disconnect(self):
    await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True)
```

`RedisClusterCache` overrides `init_async_client`, the two mget paths and `test_connection` —
but **not** `disconnect()` — so the base-class dereference is always reached.

### Impact

The exception propagates out of `proxy_shutdown_event()`, so everything ordered after
`litellm.cache.disconnect()` is skipped:

| line | step | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| 838-840 | `flush_gateway_requests()`, `prisma_client.disconnect()` | ✅ run before the crash |
| 843 | `litellm.cache.disconnect()` | 💥 raises |
| 845 | `jwt_handler.close()` | ❌ skipped |
| 848 | `db_writer_client.close()` | ❌ skipped |
| 852 | `shutdown_billing_metrics_recorder()` | ❌ skipped |
| 856 | langfuse flush | ❌ skipped |
| 868 | `cleanup_router_config_variables()` | ❌ skipped |

Prisma closing first bounds the damage, but the skipped billing flush is data loss by your own
comment at `proxy_server.py:851-852`: *"final flush of billable-request counts: without it, up
to one export interval of enterprise billing data is dropped on every restart."* Anyone running
cluster mode with enterprise billing or langfuse loses that on every restart.

### Reproduce

1. Point the proxy at any cluster-mode Redis (e.g. ElastiCache Serverless, which is always cluster-mode) and set `REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES`.
2. Start the proxy, then send SIGTERM.
3. Shutdown raises instead of completing.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

 1.97.0 (also reproduces on 1.96.2 — same code, only a Final annotation differs)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale:
This is a deterministic crash: RedisCache.disconnect() dereferences async_redis_conn_pool without a None check, and in cluster mode that pool is always None by design, causing an unhandled AttributeError on every proxy shutdown. This matches documented/expected behavior violation (shutdown should complete cleanly) rather than missing docs, so it is a bug, not docs. It causes skipped shutdown steps including billing metrics flush (data loss) and langfuse flush for any user running Redis cluster mode - a widely used deployment pattern (e.g., ElastiCache Serverless is always cluster mode). This is reproducible 100% of the time with clear repro steps and root cause identified, plus a suggested fix. It's not a security issue, not a question, and the code contradicts the intended "graceful shutdown" contract. Impact: affects a distinct but plausibly common subset of users (those using cluster mode Redis), with data loss (billing metrics) as a consequence, but there's no complete workaround mentioned by the reporter (other than avoiding cluster mode) and it deterministically breaks shutdown, causing data loss. This pushes toward P1 given the data-loss angle and clear reproduction, but affects only a subset (cluster-mode Redis users) — not "most users on a current release" but a fairly common configuration. Given the data loss and complete deterministic failure with no stated workaround, but restricted to a specific configuration, P2 seems appropriate as baseline, however the "data loss" impact plus complete shutdown breakage push this higher — but since it's not affecting most users only cluster-mode users, and there's no regression indicated, I'll set P2 given subset affected, no workaround stated, but not "broken for most users" threshold for P0/P1.
Since there's a clear reproduction, well-specified root cause and suggested fix already provided, this can be routed directly to the caching/redis module without further clarification — needs_human is false.

items.title: [Bug]: chat->responses bridge emits output_text input items without required 'annotations' field (strict providers like Azure reject with 400)
items.body:
### What happened?

When a `/chat/completions` request for a gpt-5.x model contains **both `tools` and `reasoning_effort`**, LiteLLM correctly bridges the request to the Responses API (the upstream chat endpoint rejects that combination with *"Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported ... Please use /v1/responses instead"*).

However, the bridge converts assistant **history** messages into `output_text` content blocks **without the `annotations` field**:

```python
# litellm/completion_extras/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py
def _convert_content_str_to_input_text(self, content: str, role: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if role == "user" or role == "system" or role == "tool":
        return {"type": "input_text", "text": content}
    else:
        return {"type": "output_text", "text": content}   # <-- no "annotations"
```

Per the OpenAI spec, `annotations` is **required** on `output_text` items passed as input. See the official openai-python SDK type ([response_output_text_param.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response_output_text_param.py)):

```python
class ResponseOutputTextParam(TypedDict, total=False):
    annotations: Required[Iterable[Annotation]]   # Required
    text: Required[str]
    type: Required[Literal["output_text"]]
```

OpenAI's own endpoint is lenient about the missing field, but stricter spec-conformant providers (e.g. **Azure AI Foundry `/openai/v1`**) reject the bridged request with 400:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_payload",
    "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing",
    "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations",
    "type": "invalid_request_error"
  }
}
```

Every odd `input[N]` index in the error corresponds to an assistant history message, so any multi-turn conversation (2nd request onward) fails. First requests succeed because there is no assistant history yet. This breaks agentic clients (OpenCode, etc.) that always send `tools` + `reasoning_effort`.

### Reproduction

Proxy config: `openai/gpt-5.x` model with `api_base` pointing to an Azure AI Foundry v1 endpoint (`https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<proj>/openai/v1`).

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-5.x-deployment",
    "reasoning_effort": "medium",
    "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_time","description":"get time","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{}}}}],
    "messages": [
      {"role":"user","content":"say ok"},
      {"role":"assistant","content":"ok"},
      {"role":"user","content":"again"}
    ]
  }'
```

Matrix (all against the same deployment):

| payload | result |
|---|---|
| multi-turn only | 200 OK (no bridge) |
| multi-turn + `reasoning_effort` | 200 OK (no bridge) |
| multi-turn + `tools` | 200 OK (no bridge) |
| multi-turn + `tools` + `reasoning_effort` | **400 annotations error** (bridged) |

The value of `reasoning_effort` doesn't matter (`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high` all fail).

### Proposed fix

One line — always emit the field, empty array when there are no annotations:

```python
        return {"type": "output_text", "text": content, "annotations": []}
```

(The list-content path `_convert_content_to_responses_format` should likewise preserve/emit `annotations` on `output_text` items.)

Related (opposite direction, already fixed): #18378 / #18754 handled responses→chat annotation preservation; this issue is about the chat→responses **request** direction.

### Relevant log output

```
litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - {
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_payload",
    "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing",
    "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "details": [
      {"code": "ValidationError", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations", "type": "error"},
      {"code": "ValidationError", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[3].content[0].annotations", "type": "error"}
    ]
  }
}
```

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.88.1

gold.rationale: The chat->responses bridge violates the documented/expected OpenAI Responses API spec by omitting the required 'annotations' field on output_text items, causing strict providers (Azure AI Foundry) to reject requests with a 400 error. This is a clear code defect with a documented spec contract being violated (bug, not docs, since code behavior is wrong). It affects multi-turn conversations with tools+reasoning_effort combos, breaking agentic clients like OpenCode on Azure - a narrower but real path (subset of providers/configs) is broken, and a workaround (avoid combining tools+reasoning_effort) may partially exist though it defeats functionality. This is not a security issue. The issue includes a clear reproduction, root cause identification, and even a proposed one-line fix, so a maintainer doesn't need to investigate further - it can be routed directly to fix.

items.title: [Bug]: responses() accepts response_format and silently ignores it — no mapping to text.format, no UnsupportedParamsError
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Closest prior art is discussed at the bottom — none of it covers this.

### What happened?

`litellm.responses()` accepts `response_format=...` and silently ignores it. The call succeeds, the caller believes a JSON schema is being enforced, and it is not.

`response_format` is the spelling every other litellm surface uses, and the one you naturally reach for coming from `litellm.completion()`. On the Responses API the equivalent capability exists and works — it is spelled `text={"format": {...}}` — but the familiar name is accepted and dropped with no error, no warning, and no log.

Three requests, same prompt, same model, asking for a strict JSON schema with a top-level `flags` array (litellm 1.96.2, `gpt-5.4-mini`, 2026-08-16):

| request | outcome |
|---|---|
| no format specified | model invents its own shape: `{"ai_speak": ..., "suggestion": ...}` |
| `text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": ..., "strict": True, "schema": ...}}` | **exact requested schema** ✅ |
| `response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...}}` | call succeeds, schema **ignored** — model returns its own shape again ❌ |

Row 3 is the bug. Row 2 proves the capability is there and reachable.

### Reproduction

No API key needed — the parameter is discarded client-side, before any provider mapping or validation runs:

```python
from litellm.responses.utils import ResponsesAPIRequestUtils as R

SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {"flags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}},
    "required": ["flags"],
    "additionalProperties": False,
}

def survives(**extra):
    params = {"input": "hi", "model": "gpt-5.4-mini", "custom_llm_provider": "openai", "kwargs": {}, **extra}
    return sorted(R.get_requested_response_api_optional_param(params).keys())

print(survives(response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "Flags", "strict": True, "schema": SCHEMA}}))
# []        <-- gone, no error

print(survives(text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "Flags", "strict": True, "schema": SCHEMA}}))
# ['text']  <-- kept

print(survives(totally_made_up_param="xyz"))
# []        <-- same silent drop for any unknown key
```

Confirmed with `litellm.drop_params is False` (the default). The end-to-end version is just `litellm.responses(model="gpt-5.4-mini", input=..., response_format=...)` and observing that the returned `output_text` does not conform.

### Root cause

`responses()` has no `response_format` parameter, so it lands in `**kwargs` and then in `local_vars`:

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/responses/main.py#L907-L1022

`get_requested_response_api_optional_param()` then narrows to the keys declared on `ResponsesAPIOptionalRequestParams`:

```python
valid_keys = get_type_hints(ResponsesAPIOptionalRequestParams).keys()
non_default_params = PreProcessNonDefaultParams.base_pre_process_non_default_params(
    ...,
    default_param_values={k: None for k in valid_keys},
    ...
)
```

and `base_pre_process_non_default_params` keeps a key only if `k in default_param_values`:

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/utils.py#L3559-L3574

`response_format` is not declared on `ResponsesAPIOptionalRequestParams` (`text` is), so it is removed here — **before** `_check_valid_arg()` runs. That is what makes it silent rather than loud: the guard that exists to catch exactly this never sees the parameter.

The guard itself is fine. Hand it the parameter directly and it produces precisely the error a caller should have gotten:

```python
R._check_valid_arg(supported_params=["text", "stream"],
                   non_default_params={"response_format": {...}},
                   drop_params=False, custom_llm_provider="openai", model="gpt-5.4-mini")
# litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: openai does not support parameters:
# {'response_format': {...}}, for model=gpt-5.4-mini. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` ...
```

So litellm already implements the correct behaviour for this case — the filter order just makes it unreachable. Note this also means `drop_params=False` does not mean what it says on this path: unknown params are dropped regardless of the setting.

### Why this one misleads rather than merely surprising

Probing the capability the obvious way returns the wrong answer about the library. A caller passes `response_format`, gets a 200 and unconstrained output, and concludes the Responses API has no structured-output support — when it has full support under a different name. We shipped a code comment asserting exactly that ("the Responses API has no `response_format`"), and it got repeated into a merged PR as established fact. It took reading litellm's source to find `text.format` sitting right there, working.

A test that only asserts the call succeeds passes against the broken version, which is presumably why this survived.

### Proposed fix

Map `response_format` onto `text.format`, leaving `text` working exactly as it does today and winning when both are supplied.

This is not new machinery — it is the mapping litellm already performs for its own `text_format=` convenience parameter:

https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.96.2/litellm/responses/utils.py#L904-L936

`convert_text_format_to_text_param()` calls `type_to_response_format_param()`, which returns a `response_format`-shaped dict **unchanged** when handed one, and then reshapes it into `{"format": {type, name, schema, strict}}`. In other words the conversion from an OpenAI-style `response_format` to `text.format` is already implemented and already on the `responses()` code path; `response_format` just never gets routed into it.

One wrinkle worth handling while there: that helper indexes `["json_schema"]["name"]` unconditionally, so the non-schema forms (`{"type": "json_object"}`, `{"type": "text"}`) need a branch — those map to `{"format": {"type": "json_object"}}` and `{"format": {"type": "text"}}`. The same latent `KeyError` is reachable today via `text_format={"type": "json_object"}`.

Raising `UnsupportedParamsError` instead would also be defensible, and is strictly better than today. But given the capability exists, litellm's stated job is normalising this kind of cross-API spelling difference, and the conversion code is already written, mapping seems like the better answer. Silently accepting is the one option that misleads.

Happy to send the PR — mapping in `responses()`/`aresponses()` next to the existing `text_format` call, with tests that assert the resulting request body actually carries `text.format` (not merely that the call returns 200).

### Prior art

Checked before filing; none of these covers it:

- **#35582** — `aresponses` silently drops `stop`, same filter, same "no error, no warning". Closed **COMPLETED** on 2026-08-02, but the only comment is the reporter withdrawing it ("will handle client-side"), with no maintainer response and no code change. The mechanism was never addressed. `stop` is also weaker as a report: it arguably has no Responses API equivalent, whereas `response_format` demonstrably does.
- **#34926** (open, unanswered) — correctly fingers the same `get_requested_response_api_optional_param` filter, but asks for something different: that `allowed_openai_params` be able to preserve an arbitrary extension field (`client_metadata`) for a custom upstream. A per-deployment passthrough allowlist would not fix a first-class OpenAI parameter with a real Responses API equivalent.
- **#35677** (open) — Responses API structured output, but a genuinely different failure: `text.format` is supplied correctly and the Anthropic tool-emulation fallback leaks its envelope into `output_text`.

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

No

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

1.96.2

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: The library silently drops the response_format parameter on responses() instead of mapping it to text.format or raising UnsupportedParamsError, contrary to documented/expected behavior (and contrary to the intent of drop_params=False). This is a clear bug: the code violates the documented contract that unsupported params should raise unless drop_params=True. It affects the widely-used core Responses API path (structured output) across providers, silently producing incorrect/unconstrained output with no error — a significant correctness issue with no workaround other than using the less-discoverable text.format param (which is itself a workaround, but most callers won't know to use it). Given the shared core path is affected and this misleads users about a core feature (structured outputs) with a silent failure mode, this deserves elevated urgency. There is a workaround (use text.format directly), which would normally lower severity, but the silent failure and lack of error, plus impact on structured-output reliability for any provider under Responses API, keeps it fairly serious. I'll set P1 given it's a correctness bug on a shared/core path (silent misbehavior affecting structured output for widely-used provider openai, no warning), but a workaround exists so I will not go to P0. A clear, well-reproduced bug report with root cause and proposed fix is provided, so a maintainer doesn't need to investigate further to confirm — but the decision on how to fix (mapping strategy, precedence rules) still needs a call, so I lean needs_human=true due to the P1 designation and judgement calls involved in the exact fix path.

items.title: Security: no-auth mode when LITELLM_MASTER_KEY unset (default docker-compose does not set it)
items.body:
## Security: proxy runs with no authentication when `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` is unset; shipped docker-compose default does not set it

**Severity:** Low (CWE-306 / CWE-287)

From a read-only security survey of master @ 7a5b98e6 (2026-08-15).

### Finding
When `master_key` is None and JWT/OAuth2 auth is not configured, `_user_api_key_auth_builder` (`proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py:1476-1487`) returns an INTERNAL_USER token for ANY `api_key` value (even garbage), and `_authorize_authenticated_request` (`:2217-2230`) skips authz entirely ("No-auth dev mode"). The default `docker-compose.yml` (`:10-28`) does not set `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` (it only reads an optional `.env`), so a fresh `docker compose up` following the quickstart leaves all inference routes open to anyone who can reach port 4000, using the operator's configured upstream credentials.

### Impact
Cost abuse, quota exhaustion, DoS — free inference via the operator's paid upstream. Startup logs a CRITICAL warning, but the default compose makes this the default configuration.

### Suggested fix
- Set a generated `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in the shipped docker-compose (or fail startup when unset in non-dev mode).

gold.rationale: This report identifies an unsafe default (no-auth dev mode triggered by missing LITELLM_MASTER_KEY) combined with a shipped docker-compose.yml that does not set the key, resulting in a plausible exploit: anyone reaching port 4000 gets unauthenticated access to inference routes using the operator's paid upstream credentials. This is an unsafe default with a plausible exploit path, so it takes precedence as security per the category rules. Impact is real (cost abuse/DoS) but requires network access to the proxy and is called out as "Low" severity by the reporter, and a CRITICAL warning is already logged at startup — so it's not a full P0 (no widespread active exploitation, and it is a known warned condition), but it does affect a default configuration path used by many following the quickstart, warranting elevated urgency. This is a security issue affecting the default setup for potentially many users with no immediate workaround other than manually setting the key, so P1 is appropriate. Security issues always require human judgement per the needs_human rule.

items.title: [Bug]: Gemini TTS via /v1/audio/speech is never spend-tracked on the proxy (no spend log, key spend stays 0)
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

Gemini text-to-speech requests sent through the proxy's `POST /v1/audio/speech` return audio (200) but never show up in spend logs, never increment the virtual key's spend, and never count against budgets. OpenAI TTS through the same endpoint, same proxy, and same key is tracked fine, so this is specific to the Gemini path (and, by the same mechanism, any TTS provider that is served by translating the speech request into a chat completion under the hood)

Expected: a `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` call priced at $0.30/M in and $2.50/M out shows a spend-log row with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero `spend`, and the key's `spend` moves, exactly like `openai/tts-1` does

Root cause, for whoever picks this up: the speech entrypoint takes `metadata` as a named argument, then builds the litellm params it hands to the speech-to-completion bridge from the remaining kwargs, so `metadata` arrives there as `None`. The bridge spreads those params into the inner completion call while reusing the outer request's logging object, and the completion call overwrites that shared object's `metadata` with `None`. By the time the proxy's spend callback runs it finds no key, user, or team on the request and skips the write. Debug logs show it directly: the Gemini call logs `user_api_key None, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None`, the OpenAI call right after it logs the hashed key

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer whose app generates speech with Gemini through the gateway sees every call at $0 and their key budget never moves

1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts", "input": "spend tracking check", "voice": "Kore"}` using their virtual key and get 200 with `audio/wav` bytes back
2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech with `{"model": "openai/tts-1", "input": "spend tracking check", "voice": "alloy"}` using the same key and get 200 with `audio/mpeg` bytes back
3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs (or GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs) and only the OpenAI request is listed, at $0.00027; the Gemini request is missing entirely
4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info with their key shows `"spend": 0.00027`, only the OpenAI call, so a max budget on that key never trips no matter how much Gemini audio they generate

After a (hypothetical) fix: both TTS calls are logged and billed to the key

1. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech for `gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts` and get 200 with `audio/wav` bytes back
2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/audio/speech for `openai/tts-1` and get 200 with `audio/mpeg` bytes back
3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs lists both requests, the Gemini one with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero spend computed from its input and audio output tokens
4. GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the key's `spend` as the sum of both calls, and a key max budget now trips on Gemini audio too

### Proof the bug occurs

Config the proxy ran with (`GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and `DATABASE_URL` set in the environment, `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`):

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts
    litellm_params:
      model: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts
      api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY
  - model_name: openai/tts-1
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/tts-1
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY
general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
```

Version or commit: `litellm_internal_staging` at 7a5b98e6a9 (v1.98.0), booted with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 41873 --detailed_debug`

Commands and their full output (real Gemini and OpenAI calls):

```
$ KEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:41873/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias":"tts-spend-repro-3"}' | jq -r .key)

$ curl -s -o speech.wav -D - -X POST http://localhost:41873/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts","input":"spend tracking check","voice":"Kore"}' | grep -i -E "^HTTP|x-litellm-call-id|content-type"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-litellm-call-id: ab71b16a-e469-437f-8859-562e1c8cb3ef
content-type: audio/wav
$ ls -la speech.wav | awk '{print $5" bytes"}'
154170 bytes

$ curl -s -o speech.mp3 -D - -X POST http://localhost:41873/v1/audio/speech -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"openai/tts-1","input":"spend tracking check","voice":"alloy"}' | grep -i -E "^HTTP|x-litellm-call-id|content-type"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-litellm-call-id: 6dcf0e92-9d26-43c6-9999-ede7aaaecaf1
content-type: audio/mpeg

$ sleep 15; curl -s "http://localhost:41873/spend/logs" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c '.[] | {request_id, model, call_type, spend}'
{"request_id":"6dcf0e92-9d26-43c6-9999-ede7aaaecaf1","model":"openai/tts-1","call_type":"aspeech","spend":0.00027}

$ curl -s "http://localhost:41873/key/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" | jq -c '.info | {key_alias, spend}'
{"key_alias":"tts-spend-repro-3","spend":0.00027}

$ curl -s "http://localhost:41873/v1/model/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | jq -c '.data[] | {model_name, input_cost_per_token: .model_info.input_cost_per_token, output_cost_per_token: .model_info.output_cost_per_token}'
{"model_name":"gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts","input_cost_per_token":3E-7,"output_cost_per_token":0.0000025}
{"model_name":"openai/tts-1","input_cost_per_token":null,"output_cost_per_token":null}
```

So the Gemini model is priced, the call succeeded, and the spend log has only the OpenAI row. The proxy's own debug log for the two calls, in order:

```
01:56:54 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_track_cost_callback.py:249 - user_api_key None, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None
01:56:56 - LiteLLM Proxy:DEBUG: proxy_track_cost_callback.py:249 - user_api_key d628805a57f5b935deab509bb849d9e7761e27681d714c191eee3336135a1f10, user_id None, team_id None, end_user_id None
```

The same happens with the master key and with the newer `gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview` (checked at #36788's head 32917b07fc)

### What a fix PR should look like

- `litellm/main.py`, `speech()`: pass the named `metadata` (and the other named args the bridge needs) into `get_litellm_params(...)` so the litellm params handed to `speech_to_completion_bridge_handler.speech` carry the request metadata instead of `None`; alternatively have `litellm/endpoints/speech/speech_to_completion_bridge/transformation.py` `transform_request` read `metadata` off the logging object's existing litellm params and forward it, so the inner completion never clobbers what the outer request set
- Whichever way, make sure the outer `aspeech` success handler ends up with the request's `metadata` and a non-zero `response_cost` in its kwargs, since the proxy's cost callback reads both from there
- Regression test in a new `tests/test_litellm/endpoints/speech/speech_to_completion_bridge/test_handler.py` (no mapped test exists yet for the bridge; `tests/test_litellm/test_main.py` also works for the `speech()` side): call `aspeech` for a `gemini/...-tts` model with `metadata={"user_api_key": "..."}` and a mocked completion, assert the success callback's `kwargs["litellm_params"]["metadata"]` still holds `user_api_key`; a second assertion that the same holds for the OpenAI path keeps the two in lockstep
- Out of scope: pricing of TTS models (already correct in `/v1/model/info`), and the `x-litellm-response-cost` header, which is empty for every `/v1/audio/speech` call and can be its own follow-up
- Proof for the fix PR: the exact commands above against a live proxy at the fix commit, showing a Gemini row in `/spend/logs` with `call_type: aspeech` and non-zero `spend`, and `/key/info` `spend` equal to the sum of both calls

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

litellm_internal_staging @ 7a5b98e6a9 (v1.98.0)

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This is a clear, well-documented bug: Gemini (and other chat-completion-bridged) TTS calls through /v1/audio/speech are not spend-tracked because metadata is dropped/overwritten as None when the speech request is translated into a chat completion call internally. The reporter identifies the root cause precisely and provides full reproduction steps, debug logs, and comparison with the working OpenAI TTS path. This affects billing/spend accuracy and budget enforcement, which is a core proxy function (spend tracking is a widely-used, shared core path), and impacts any provider that uses this speech-to-completion bridge, not just Gemini. There's no workaround since spend tracking silently fails. This is not a security vulnerability, not a docs issue, and not a feature request - it's broken behavior in an existing supported code path. Given the impact on billing/budget enforcement (a widely-used core proxy feature) with no workaround, and affecting multiple providers via the shared bridge mechanism, this warrants P1 severity. It needs human review because it's a P1-level issue with a claimed root cause that should be verified/confirmed by a maintainer before routing, and it involves nontrivial internal logic (shared logging object mutation) requiring judgement to fix correctly across providers.

items.title: GET /spend/logs has no pagination and OOM-kills the proxy on a large LiteLLM_SpendLogs
items.body:
### What happens

`GET /spend/logs` with no query parameters fetches every row of
`LiteLLM_SpendLogs` into memory. On a table of ~110k rows (~371 MB on disk) this
exhausts the container and the kernel kills it:

```
reason   = OOMKilled
exitCode = 137
limit    = 4Gi
```

The proxy is unavailable for about a minute while it restarts. In our deployment
that proxy fronts all model traffic, so a single admin API call takes every model
in the cluster offline.

Version: **v1.90.0**, PostgreSQL backend.

### Why it is not avoidable by the caller

`view_spend_logs` accepts no pagination parameters at all — there is no `page`,
`limit`, or `page_size` in the signature, only filters that all default to
`None`:

```python
async def view_spend_logs(
    api_key:    Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    user_id:    Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    request_id: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    start_date: Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    end_date:   Optional[str] = fastapi.Query(default=None, ...),
    summarize:  bool          = fastapi.Query(default=True,  ...),
    ...
)
```

and the query is issued with no row cap:

```python
data = await SpendLogsRepository(prisma_client).table.find_many(
    where=filter_query,
    order={...},
)
```

`find_many` is called without `take`. A caller who passes no filters therefore
cannot bound the result; the only way to stay safe is to know in advance not to
call the endpoint.

### The paginated endpoints already exist

`/spend/logs/v2` and `/spend/logs/ui` do the right thing:

```python
page:      int = fastapi.Query(default=1, ge=1)
page_size: int = fastapi.Query(default=50, description="Number of items per page", ge=1, le=100)
```

and the admin UI calls those, not the legacy path. So the unbounded behaviour is
isolated to the v1 endpoint — which is what makes this look like an oversight
rather than a design choice.

### Suggested fix

Any of these would close it; the first seems closest to existing behaviour:

1. Add `page` / `page_size` to `view_spend_logs` and pass `take`/`skip` through
   to `find_many`, mirroring the v2 endpoint.
2. Apply a server-side default cap (e.g. `take=1000`) when no `request_id` is
   given, and document that the endpoint truncates.
3. Deprecate `/spend/logs` in favour of `/spend/logs/v2` and have it return a
   `400` when called without filters, pointing at the paginated path.

### Reproducing

Populate `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` with a few hundred thousand rows, set a container
memory limit in the low gigabytes, then:

```
GET /spend/logs
Authorization: Bearer <master key>
```

The request does not return; the connection closes when the process is killed.

### Notes

- Retention does not fix this on its own. `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`
  bounds growth over time, but a bursty workload can add tens of thousands of
  rows in a single day, so the table can cross the threshold within any
  retention window.
- We mitigated locally by blocking the exact path at the ingress. That is
  possible only because the UI uses the `/ui` and `/v2` variants; it is a
  workaround for an operator, not a fix.

gold.rationale: This is a clear bug: an admin API endpoint (/spend/logs) violates reasonable expected behaviour by loading an unbounded number of rows into memory with no pagination, causing an OOM crash that takes down the entire proxy (all model traffic). The report includes a clear reproduction, code references showing the missing `take` cap, and shows related endpoints already implement proper pagination, confirming this is an oversight rather than by design. This affects availability broadly (proxy serving all models goes down), with no workaround other than blocking the endpoint at the ingress (an operator-side mitigation, not a fix), so it should be raised. Given it's a shared/core proxy path affecting all users of that deployment and causing a full outage of model traffic for about a minute, this is severe — a major, widely used core path (spend logging under admin API) is broken with no built-in workaround, warranting P1. It does not rise to P0 since it isn't a widespread issue for all users by default in every deployment (requires large table) and no data loss occurs, just temporary unavailability. Because this is P1, it requires human judgement per policy (P0/P1 requires human look), and also because reproduction/confirmation of severity is worth validating before routing/fix approach decision (three suggested fixes represent a product/design choice).

items.title: [Bug]: Admin UI session cookie is a non-HttpOnly JWT carrying the caller's proxy key
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

The Admin UI login sets a `token` cookie holding a JWT whose `key` claim is the caller's real proxy key, and the cookie is not marked `HttpOnly`. For a proxy admin signing in with `UI_USERNAME` / `UI_PASSWORD` or through SSO, that means a full-privilege `sk-...` key sits in `document.cookie`, readable by any script running on `/ui`, for the whole 8h cookie lifetime.

Two things make it worse than a normal session cookie:

The key keeps working outside the browser. Anything that can read the cookie can paste the decoded key into `curl` and mint new keys, read spend, or call models, with no session involved.

Logout does not revoke it. The dashboard clears cookies client-side, so a key that was copied before logout stays valid until its own expiry.

I would expect the browser to hold an opaque session identifier that the proxy resolves server-side, in an `HttpOnly` cookie, with a logout route that drops the session on the server.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the proxy with any config that sets a master key, for example

```yaml
model_list: []

general_settings:
  master_key: sk-1234
```

2. Log in the way the Admin UI does, and look at the cookie it sets

```
$ curl -si -X POST http://localhost:4000/login -d 'username=admin&password=sk-1234' | grep -i '^set-cookie'
set-cookie: token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjoiZGVmYXVsdF91c2VyX2lkIiwia2V5Ijoic2steHh4eHh4...<truncated>; Path=/; SameSite=lax
```

No `HttpOnly` flag, so `document.cookie` in the devtools console on http://localhost:4000/ui/ returns the same string.

3. Decode the middle segment

```
$ echo "$TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | python -m json.tool
{
  "user_id": "default_user_id",
  "key": "sk-<the admin's real proxy key>",
  "user_role": "proxy_admin",
  "login_method": "username_password",
  "auth_header_name": "Authorization",
  "server_root_path": "",
  "exp": 1786805817
}
```

4. Use that key from outside the browser

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY_FROM_COOKIE" \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"minted-outside-the-browser"}'
{
  "key": "sk-...",
  "key_alias": "minted-outside-the-browser",
  "expires": null
}
```

5. Log out in the UI, then repeat step 4 with the same key; it still mints keys

### Relevant log output

```shell
POST /login HTTP/1.1" 303 See Other
POST /key/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 OK   # using the key decoded out of the login cookie
```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

UI Dashboard

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0 (reproduced on `litellm_internal_staging` at 423b791ee0)

### Possible direction

I have a working change locally that swaps the JWT for an opaque `sso_<hex>` handle stored in the cache the `login_code` exchange already uses, delivered in an `HttpOnly` `SameSite=Lax` cookie, plus `/sso/session/me` for identity and `/sso/session/logout` for server-side revocation, with a credential-free `litellm_ui_session=1` marker so the dashboard can still tell a session exists. Happy to open a PR if that direction sounds right to you.

gold.rationale: The Admin UI session cookie embeds the user's actual proxy master/admin key in a JWT claim, and the cookie lacks HttpOnly, exposing a full-privilege key to any script running on the page (XSS or malicious extension) and allowing it to be used outside the browser entirely. Additionally, logout does not revoke the key server-side, so a leaked/copied key remains valid for its full lifetime. This is a credential exposure / unsafe default with a clear, plausible exploit path (script reads document.cookie, extracts a live sk- key, uses it directly against the API to mint new keys or read spend), which meets the security category bar and takes precedence over bug framing. It affects the shared UI/auth path used by all proxy admins and SSO users, has no workaround for the underlying design flaw (aside from not using the UI), and there is a data/credential exposure risk with no mitigation — this warrants P0. Given it's a security issue, needs_human must be true for a maintainer to assess and validate the proposed fix (opaque session token direction) even though the reporter offers a PR.

items.title: Feature proposal: optional GoAnyAPI provider for SEO data tools
items.body:
Hi — I run GoAnyAPI and would be interested in contributing an optional provider integration for SEO data workflows.
