This describes new functionality that does not yet exist, so it falls under "feature." There is no evidence of broader community demand beyond the single requester (who is the vendor themselves), so per the rules, it defaults to P3 despite the detailed write-up. It's a well-specified feature proposal with an offer to contribute a PR, which is a product-direction decision a maintainer should weigh in on before proceeding, but it can also reasonably be queued as a feature request for later consideration. Given it involves a product-direction call about whether to add a new optional provider (not just a code change), maintainer judgement is warranted.

items.title: AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url doesn't dedup trailing /v1 in api_base (yields /v1/v1/messages), unlike openai_like/deepseek siblings
items.body:
### What happened

`AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` appends `/v1/messages` to a custom `api_base` without deduplicating a trailing `/v1`:

```python
# litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/transformation.py (~line 227)
api_base = AnthropicModelInfo.get_api_base(api_base) or "https://api.anthropic.com"
if not api_base.endswith("/v1/messages"):
    api_base = f"{api_base}/v1/messages"
```

So a deployment resolving to `custom_llm_provider: anthropic` with `api_base: https://host/v1` produces `https://host/v1/v1/messages`, which 404s at the provider.

Every sibling Anthropic-messages config already handles this:

- `OpenAILikeAnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` (`litellm/llms/openai_like/messages/transformation.py`) does `rstrip("/")` → return if endswith `/v1/messages` → `removesuffix("/v1")` → append, with test coverage in `tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/messages/test_openai_like_anthropic_messages_transformation.py` asserting `https://host/v1 → https://host/v1/messages`.
- `DeepSeek`'s messages config (`litellm/llms/deepseek/messages/transformation.py`) has the same normalization.

Only the Anthropic config lacks it. Users hit this when pointing an `anthropic/`-prefixed model at an Anthropic-compatible gateway whose base already ends in `/v1` — see discussion #36651 for a real-world report (Claude Code → LiteLLM → Groq/NIM, where a misconfigured entry surfaces exactly this shape).

### Expected behavior

`api_base: https://host/v1` should yield `https://host/v1/messages`, consistent with the openai_like and deepseek configs.

### Proposed fix

Mirror the openai_like normalization in `AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url` (two lines), plus parametrized tests matching the openai_like test table. PR incoming.

gold.rationale: This is a clear, well-documented bug: AnthropicMessagesConfig.get_complete_url fails to dedup a trailing /v1 in api_base, producing malformed URLs (/v1/v1/messages) that 404, unlike sibling configs (openai_like, deepseek) which already handle this correctly. The code behaves inconsistently with documented/expected behavior and with sibling implementations. It affects users pointing anthropic-prefixed models at gateways with /v1 suffix (e.g., Claude Code -> LiteLLM -> Groq/NIM per linked discussion), which is a real but narrow path. A workaround exists (avoid trailing /v1 in api_base config), and the fix is small and well-specified with a PR incoming, so it does not need maintainer judgement before routing.

items.title: [Bug]: SSO and JWT email matching can take over an existing proxy admin
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate

### What happened?

When an SSO or JWT subject does not match an existing `user_id` or `sso_user_id`, LiteLLM falls back to a case-insensitive email lookup. A matching row is returned even if it already has a different `sso_user_id`, and LiteLLM schedules an update that overwrites that id with the new subject

The SSO path then inherits the matched row's stored role when the identity provider did not supply a LiteLLM role. The JWT path checks the matched row's role directly. A different identity-provider subject that can present an existing privileged email can therefore inherit `PROXY_ADMIN` and durably rebind the victim's `sso_user_id`

There is no shared requirement that the email claim is verified, no refusal when the row already has a different SSO subject, and no protection for administrative roles

Expected behavior is that email linking is allowed only for a verified email on an explicitly unlinked or invited row. A row already bound to another subject, especially a proxy admin, must not be silently rebound

### User Flow

Before a fix: a second identity-provider subject can become an existing proxy admin by presenting the same email

1. An administrator already has a LiteLLM dashboard account bound to SSO subject `admin-subject`
2. A different trusted identity-provider subject authenticates at `GET https://litellm-domain/sso/callback` with the administrator's email in its claims
3. LiteLLM misses by the new subject, finds the administrator row by email, and overwrites its `sso_user_id`
4. The new subject is redirected into `https://litellm-domain/ui/` with the stored `proxy_admin` role
5. The new subject can call `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate` and other administrator routes
6. The original administrator can be locked out because their row is now bound to the different subject
7. The attacker can access other users' keys and management data that their original identity should never reach

After a fix: a subject mismatch cannot silently link to a privileged or already-bound row

1. The same administrator account remains bound to `admin-subject`
2. The different identity-provider subject authenticates with the same email claim
3. LiteLLM detects that the row is already bound to another subject, or that the email is not verified
4. `GET https://litellm-domain/sso/callback` returns a 403 or creates a separate non-admin user according to policy
5. The new subject cannot call `POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate`
6. The original administrator remains able to sign in with `admin-subject`
7. The second subject cannot read or modify any other user's management objects

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup:

```yaml
general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

Enable Generic OIDC, SAML, or JWT auth. Existing database row:

```json
{
  "user_id": "admin-user",
  "user_email": "admin@example.test",
  "sso_user_id": "admin-subject",
  "user_role": "proxy_admin"
}
```

Version / commit:

```text
v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff
```

Current shared fuzzy-link code:

```python
if response is None and user_email is not None:
    response = await user_table.find_first(
        where={"user_email": {"equals": user_email, "mode": "insensitive"}},
        include={"organization_memberships": True},
    )

    if response is not None and sso_user_id is not None:
        asyncio.create_task(
            user_table.update(
                where={"user_id": response.user_id},
                data={"sso_user_id": sso_user_id},
            )
        )
```

The repository's existing test encodes the unsafe rebinding contract. It starts with a row whose SSO id is `sso_123`, looks it up by email for `new_sso_456`, and expects the update to the new id

Audit command and output:

```shell
$ uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_auth_checks.py::test_get_fuzzy_user_object
============================== 1 passed ==============================
```

The current SSO role resolution uses the database role when the SSO response does not supply a LiteLLM role. The JWT auth builder also calls `get_user_object` with the presented subject and email, then treats a returned `PROXY_ADMIN` row as admin

A live third-party identity provider was not used because reproducing against a real account would modify authentication state. The test and source path confirm the email match, subject overwrite, and role inheritance without external side effects

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.98.0, commit 46ffc2ab7d4b29889b54f9ccefd78f995a0e53ff

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This report describes an authentication/authorization bypass: a mismatched SSO/JWT subject can be silently linked to an existing user row via case-insensitive email match, without verifying subject binding or email verification, allowing privilege escalation to proxy_admin and account takeover. This is a plausible exploit path affecting auth bypass and privilege escalation, which per the rules takes precedence as security regardless of it being framed as a bug. It affects the shared core auth path used by SSO and JWT across all providers, impacting confidentiality and integrity broadly, with no workaround - clear P0. Requires maintainer judgement to assess and design correct linking policy (verified email + explicit invite/unlink requirement), and to weigh backward compatibility with existing test asserting old behavior, so needs_human is true.

This qualifies as a bug, and given it's a complete failure to start (affects most/all users on the current release, no workaround), it's high urgency - regression + core path affected pushes it up further. Requires maintainer judgement to fix the FastAPI version pinning/compatibility issue, and reproduction may need confirming exact FastAPI version combos.

items.title: [Bug]: GET /health returns extra_headers and aws_session_token in plaintext
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

Related, not a duplicate: #18818 fixed masking of `extra_headers` on `/model/info`. `GET /health` is a different sanitizer. It still returns those values in full. `api_key` is stripped (CVE-2025-11203 class). `extra_headers` and `aws_session_token` were never added to that strip list.

### What happened?

LiteLLM 1.96.2. No master key. A deployment in `config.yaml` has `extra_headers` (Azure `api-key`, Google `x-goog-api-key`, a Bearer token) and `aws_session_token`.

`GET /health` returns those values in plaintext on the healthy (or unhealthy) row. `api_key` is absent. `api_base` is absent for a non-admin caller. The extra headers stay.

This was reproduced with fake `CANARY_*` strings, not real provider keys. A live proxy with a normal `api_key: os.environ/...` and no `extra_headers` does not echo the resolved key on `/model/info` (`api_key` is popped). The hole is specifically fields that are not `api_key`.

Expected: `/health` should omit or mask `extra_headers`, `headers`, and `aws_session_token` the same way it already omits `api_key`.

### User Flow

Before a (hypothetical) fix: a tenant who can call `/health` can read the admin's upstream credentials out of the JSON.

1. The proxy admin puts provider auth in `litellm_params.extra_headers` (and optionally `aws_session_token`) in `config.yaml`, then starts the proxy on `http://127.0.0.1:4000`.
2. Any caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health` with no `Authorization` header (default install, no master key).
3. HTTP 200. The `healthy_endpoints` (or `unhealthy_endpoints`) row contains `extra_headers.Authorization`, `extra_headers.x-goog-api-key`, `extra_headers.api-key`, and `aws_session_token` in full.
4. That caller can take those values and call the provider directly, bypassing the proxy.

After a (hypothetical) fix: the same `/health` call still reports healthy/unhealthy, but those secret fields are gone or masked.

1. The proxy admin uses the same `config.yaml` and starts the same proxy.
2. The same caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health`.
3. HTTP 200. The row still has `model` and health status. It does not contain the `extra_headers` values or `aws_session_token`.
4. That caller cannot recover the admin's upstream credentials from `/health`.

### Proof the bug occurs

Config / setup the proxy ran with:

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: mock
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/mockmodel
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9996/v1
      api_key: sk-x-CANARY_DEPLOYMENT_API_KEY
      extra_headers:
        Authorization: Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION
        x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE
        api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY
      aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE
```

The backend at `127.0.0.1:9996` is a local OpenAI-compatible stub that returns HTTP 200 so the row lands in `healthy_endpoints`. The leak is the proxy copying `litellm_params` into the `/health` body. It does not depend on a real provider key.

You can drop the stub: point `api_base` at `http://127.0.0.1:1`. The health check fails, and the same fields still appear under `unhealthy_endpoints`. No API key required.

Version or commit: LiteLLM **1.96.2**

Commands and their full output:

```
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health
```

```json
{
  "healthy_endpoints": [
    {
      "model": "openai/mockmodel",
      "extra_headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION",
        "x-goog-api-key": "CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE",
        "api-key": "CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY"
      },
      "aws_session_token": "CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE"
    }
  ],
  "unhealthy_endpoints": [],
  "healthy_count": 1,
  "unhealthy_count": 0
}
```

`api_key` is not in that object. `GET /v1/models` and `GET /health/liveliness` do not contain the canaries.

Copy-paste repro, no keys, no stub:

```yaml
# leak.yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: demo
    litellm_params:
      model: openai/gpt-4o-mini
      api_base: http://127.0.0.1:1
      api_key: sk-not-a-real-key
      extra_headers:
        x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE
        api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY
      aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE
```

```
litellm --config leak.yaml --port 4000 --host 127.0.0.1
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health
```

The canaries show up on the unhealthy row.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.96.2

gold.rationale: The /health endpoint leaks sensitive credentials (extra_headers containing Authorization/API keys, and aws_session_token) in plaintext to any caller, including unauthenticated ones when no master key is set. This is a credential exposure vulnerability with a clear, low-effort exploit path (simple curl request), analogous to a previously patched CVE for a different endpoint (/model/info). This fits the security category definition exactly: credential exposure with a plausible exploit path, which takes precedence over bug classification. Given it's a live credential leak affecting any deployment using extra_headers or aws_session_token in config, and there's no workaround mentioned (masking is missing entirely, not configurable), this is high urgency. It affects a subset of users (those using extra_headers/aws_session_token specifically) but the exploit is trivial and impactful (full credential exposure allowing direct provider API bypass), matching P0 criteria for security vulnerabilities with plausible exploit paths and no workaround. Security issues always need human review per policy.

items.title: /models endpoint response shape breaks OpenAI Codex CLI's model discovery
items.body:
Codex CLI (OpenAI's coding agent) discovers available models by calling
`<base_url>/models` on its configured provider and expects a response
shaped like:

    {"models": [{"id": "...", ...}, ...]}

LiteLLM's proxy returns the standard OpenAI shape instead:

    {"data": [{"id": "...", ...}, ...]}

Because of the mismatch, Codex's decode fails every session
("failed to refresh available models"), and Codex silently falls back to
its own bundled, static model catalogue instead of the models the gateway
actually serves. In practice this means Codex's `/model` picker can offer
models the gateway doesn't have and hide ones it does.

This is the same category of issue #27180 fixed for Claude Code, which
added an Anthropic-native `/v1/models` response format so Claude Code's
own discovery would work against the proxy. Codex needs the equivalent:
either an alternate response shape when the request looks like it's
coming from Codex, or a Codex-specific route that returns `{"models": [...]}`.

One added wrinkle for a full fix: OpenAI's own model list ships large
(~17k-char) system prompts per model (`base_instructions`), so a
Codex-shaped `/models` response would need to include that data for each
entry to fully match what Codex expects from its native provider.

Happy to provide more detail on the exact request Codex sends if useful.

gold.rationale: This is a well-specified compatibility issue: the proxy's /models endpoint returns OpenAI-shaped {"data": [...]} but Codex CLI expects {"models": [...]}, causing Codex's model discovery to fail and silently fall back to a stale bundled catalogue. This is a functional mismatch versus expected/integration behavior (analogous to the prior Claude Code fix, #27180), so it's a bug in integration behavior rather than purely missing docs. It doesn't rise to a security issue. There is precedent (a similar fix was already made for Claude Code), showing this is a recognized category of problem affecting agent integrations, but it's scoped to a specific client (Codex) rather than a core provider or broad user base, and a workaround (bundled static catalog) exists, albeit degraded. This suggests P2: narrower integration affected, workaround (fallback catalogue) exists, but is a real functional defect for Codex users of the proxy. It requires product/implementation judgement (new route or conditional response shape, plus handling the base_instructions field), and since it's a design decision on how to add Codex support, a maintainer should weigh in before implementation just as they did for Claude Code.

items.title: [Bug]: OAUTH_TOKEN_INFO_ENDPOINT is under documented and doesn't exist for MSFT
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

As a customer / premium user, while trying to setup OAuth2 authentication on our proxy, I ran into errors with [OAUTH_TOKEN_INFO_ENDPOINT](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/f64479e74d9d20d0edc806139b36d2a0db55a28c/litellm/proxy/auth/oauth2_check.py#L139) not being set. [Looking at the website](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/oauth2), this requirement is barely documented, and the expected value is not specified.

As we are using Microsoft Entra, I went looking for the endpoint, helped by the comment referencing the RFC (thanks!). Turns out [Microsoft does not implement such an endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1359899/validate-introspect-access-token).

Finally, third and most minor issue, being able to configure this via the config file would be welcome, instead of having to split configuration between config and environment.

### User Flow

```yaml
general_settings:
  enable_oauth2_auth: true
```

### Proof the bug occurs

See comments above

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v1.94.1

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: The issue reports that OAUTH_TOKEN_INFO_ENDPOINT is under-documented (docs page barely mentions it) and that for Microsoft Entra this endpoint doesn't exist, meaning the documented OAuth2 setup doesn't work for a widely-used provider (Azure/Microsoft Entra). This is a mix of a docs gap and a functional gap (code doesn't support providers without an introspection endpoint), plus a feature request to allow config-file based configuration. Since the core problem is that the OAuth2 flow doesn't work as expected for a major identity provider (Microsoft Entra), and the code's reliance on an RFC introspection endpoint contradicts real-world provider behavior, this leans toward a bug (code/behavior doesn't match reasonable expectations for OAuth2 support) rather than pure docs, since fixing it requires code changes to support providers lacking introspection endpoints. Microsoft Entra is a widely used auth provider, so this affects a meaningful subset of proxy OAuth2 users setting up enterprise SSO, though a workaround (using a different token validation method) may exist. Given the multiple facets (docs, bug, feature) bundled in one issue, and that it affects enterprise auth setup, human triage is warranted to decide the right path.

items.title: [Bug]: Bedrock streaming silently hangs forever (zero bytes, no error, no logs) when thinking.budget_tokens > ~16.4k on adaptive-thinking-only models (Opus 4.8)
items.body:
### What happened?

Calling the proxy's Anthropic-format endpoint (`/v1/messages`) with **streaming + `thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}`** against a Bedrock model that only supports **adaptive thinking** (`eu.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, eu-north-1) produces two stacked bugs:

1. **Translation bug:** for budgets **≤ ~16.4k** LiteLLM evidently translates the classic `enabled` thinking format into something Bedrock accepts (requests stream fine, verified with streams > 5 min). For budgets **≥ 20 000** the upstream request is invalid and Bedrock instantly rejects it.
2. **Error-swallowing bug (the severe one):** that instant upstream `ValidationException` is **swallowed on the streaming path**. The client connection returns **zero bytes forever** — no `message_start`, no error event, no HTTP error, and **nothing is written to proxy logs at any level**. The connection just sits open until some middlebox kills it (in our case Azure Container Apps ingress/Envoy cuts it at 240 s with `504 stream timeout`).

Real-world impact: Claude Code's deep-thinking modes request ~32k thinking budgets, so every such request through a LiteLLM proxy to Bedrock Opus 4.8 deterministically dies as a silent ~4-minute stall ("API Error: The response stopped arriving") with no server-side trace, which makes this extremely hard to diagnose from logs.

### Reproduction

Proxy request (fails — zero bytes for 240 s, then LB timeout; on a proxy without an LB in front it presumably hangs indefinitely):

```bash
curl -s -N -X POST "$PROXY/v1/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "eu.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8",
    "max_tokens": 28000,
    "stream": true,
    "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 20000},
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Think exhaustively, then write a detailed zero-downtime Postgres partitioning migration runbook."}]
  }'
```

Measured boundary (same request, only budget varies):

| `budget_tokens` | Result |
|---|---|
| 8 000 / 16 000 / 16 400 | Streams fine (`message_start` → `message_stop`, incl. streams > 300 s) |
| 20 000 | Zero bytes, silent hang, 2/2 attempts |

Same 20k-budget payload against **direct Anthropic API** through the same proxy: streams fine (373 s, clean finish) — Anthropic accepts `enabled`, Bedrock Opus 4.8 does not.

### Root cause evidence (raw Bedrock, bypassing LiteLLM)

`boto3 invoke_model_with_response_stream` on `eu.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` with `thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N}` is rejected **instantly (0.5 s) for ANY budget** (tested 8k and 20k):

```
ValidationException: "thinking.type.enabled" is not supported for this model.
Use "thinking.type.adaptive" and "output_config.effort" to control thinking behavior.
```

With the adaptive format (`"thinking": {"type": "adaptive"}, "output_config": {"effort": "high"}`) raw Bedrock streams perfectly.

So Bedrock answers correctly and immediately in all cases — the infinite zero-byte hang happens inside LiteLLM's Bedrock streaming path when the upstream request is rejected.

### Expected behavior

1. Translate `thinking: enabled + budget_tokens` → `thinking: adaptive + output_config.effort` for adaptive-only Bedrock models across the **whole** budget range (or clamp), as apparently already happens for budgets ≤ ~16.4k.
2. Regardless of translation: an upstream 4xx during stream setup must surface to the client as an error (SSE `error` event / HTTP error) and be logged — never a silent infinite hang. This failure mode currently produces no diagnostic signal anywhere.

### Version & deployment

- LiteLLM **v1.96.2** (ghcr digest `sha256:154e23bb...`); also reproduced on ~v1.94-era `main-stable` (digest `sha256:af806882...`), so not a recent regression.
- Proxy server mode, Docker (ghcr image), `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`, model `bedrock/eu.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8`, region eu-north-1, standard AWS access-key credentials on the model entry.
- Client: Anthropic-native `/v1/messages` endpoint (Claude Code via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`).

### Relevant log output

```
(none — that is part of the bug: nothing is logged at ERROR/WARNING/INFO for the hanging request)
```

### Are you an ML Ops Team?

Yes — self-hosted LiteLLM proxy serving Claude Code developers.

gold.rationale: This is a genuine bug report affecting the Bedrock streaming path: (1) incorrect/incomplete translation of Anthropic 'enabled' thinking format to Bedrock's 'adaptive' format for budgets above ~16.4k, causing instant upstream rejection, and (2) a severe error-swallowing bug where upstream 4xx validation errors during stream setup are silently dropped, causing indefinite hangs with zero client-visible signal and no server logs. This matches the 'bug' category exactly - documented/expected behavior (successful translation, and errors surfacing to client) is violated by actual behavior. The impact is significant: it affects a widely-used provider path (Bedrock streaming with thinking-enabled requests), causes silent multi-minute hangs for any client hitting the affected budget range (like Claude Code's deep-thinking mode which requests ~32k budgets), and has no logging to aid diagnosis. This is not merely a narrow edge case - it's a systemic issue in error handling on the streaming path plus an incomplete parameter translation, both hitting the shared Bedrock invocation code. There's no confirmed workaround other than limiting budget size, which is a narrow mitigation not a real workaround for users needing higher budgets. Given it affects a widely used provider (Bedrock) and the shared streaming/error-handling path, and given the severity (silent hang, no diagnostics, in production), this warrants P1. It requires maintainer judgement to confirm reproduction and decide the best fix approach (extending translation range vs proper error surfacing), and combines two distinct problems (translation bug + error swallowing) requiring judgement about scope, so needs_human should be true.

items.title: [Bug]: OpenAI passthrough `/v1/embeddings` writes no spend log row at all — billable tokens are unattributable, and budgets under-enforce
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

---

### What happened?

**In brief:** `POST /openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings` returns 200 and consumes real billable tokens, but LiteLLM writes **no `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row at all** — not a zero-cost row, nothing. No `x-litellm-response-cost` header, and no movement in `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend`, so the spend is not booked off-ledger either. A virtual key with a hard budget can therefore spend without limit on this route.

**What I expected to happen:** the call should write a spend row with `response_cost = prompt_tokens × input_cost_per_token` and move the calling key's spend, exactly as translated `POST /v1/embeddings` does with the same key and model, and as Cohere passthrough `/v1/embed` already does.


#### Setup that triggers it

- Proxy with an OpenAI passthrough route mounted (`/openai_passthrough/{endpoint:path}`) and DB-backed spend tracking enabled.
- `POST /openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings` with any OpenAI embedding model (`text-embedding-3-small` here).
- No special flags. Nothing about this is deployment-specific — the gate is a hardcoded string-literal predicate.

#### Expected

A passthrough embeddings call that consumes billable prompt tokens should write a `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` row with `response_cost = prompt_tokens × input_cost_per_token`, exactly as the translated `POST /v1/embeddings` route does, and as the **Cohere** passthrough handler already does for `/v1/embed`.

#### Actual

No row. Not a zero-cost row — **nothing**. No `x-litellm-response-cost` header, and no movement in `LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend`, so it is not booked off-ledger either.

The mechanism is two independent hardcoded gates:

**Gate 1 — the dispatcher rejects the route before the handler is called.** `success_handler.py::_is_supported_openai_endpoint` (`main`, lines 430–434):

```python
return (
    OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler.is_openai_chat_completions_route(url_route)
    or OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler.is_openai_image_generation_route(url_route)
    or OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler.is_openai_image_editing_route(url_route)
    or OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler.is_openai_responses_route(url_route)
)
```

`/v1/embeddings` matches none of the four.

**Gate 2 — the handler has no embeddings branch.** `openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py::openai_passthrough_handler`:

```python
if not (is_chat_completions or is_image_generation or is_image_editing or is_responses):
    # For unsupported endpoints, return None to let the system fall back to generic behavior
    return {
        "result": None,
        "kwargs": kwargs,
    }
```

Note what this early return does **not** do: it never sets `kwargs["response_cost"]`. Exactly four predicates are defined (`main` lines 113, 121, 129, 137) and `grep -ic embed` over the file returns 0.

Given this input:

```json
{"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}
```

the handler returns, verbatim:

```
handler returned result = None
response_cost SET IN KWARGS: False
```

**Two independent defects here, not one:**

1. **The route is filtered out at Gate 1.** Adding an embeddings branch inside the handler would be unreachable dead code without also adding the predicate to `_is_supported_openai_endpoint`. This is precisely the line that had to be added for the Responses API.
2. **The `None` cost is then fatal, not merely zero.** Because Gate 2 returns without setting `response_cost`, it stays `None`. In `proxy_track_cost_callback.py` the escape hatch requires `standard_logging_object is None`, but that object is built unconditionally on the success path — so control reaches the `raise` of `"Cost tracking failed for model=…"`. The local `except` fires a Slack alert and calls `spend_log_error`; **it never writes a row.** This would be the next failure even after fixing (1), and it is why the observed result is *no row* rather than a *$0 row*.

The comment `# ... let the system fall back to generic behavior` is the line that admits to the masking: there is no generic cost-tracking fallback for this path, so "fall back" means "silently produce nothing."

#### Downstream effect, and how the failure is masked

The request itself succeeds — HTTP 200, real embeddings returned, real tokens billed by the provider. The failure is invisible at two layers:

1. **The logging coroutine is discarded.** The success handler is dispatched via a bare `asyncio.create_task` with no `await`, no `add_done_callback`, and no wrapping `try`. The `raise` above dies with the task and never reaches the caller.
2. **The response looks clean.** No error, and no `x-litellm-response-cost` header to be conspicuously zero — `get_custom_headers` renders the cost via `str()` then filters `{"", None, "None"}`, so a `None` cost and a `0` cost are both erased into an absent header.

So a caller would reasonably conclude the traffic was free, and any downstream export keyed off the spend row misses it entirely. **This is budget under-enforcement, not just a reporting gap.**

The asymmetry makes it sharper: `GET /openai_passthrough/v1/models` consumes **0 tokens** and still gets a row (`$0`, `model='unknown'`), because its `response_cost` resolves to `0.0` and satisfies `if response_cost is not None`. Zero-token work gets a receipt; billable work does not.

#### Scope notes — what was and wasn't tested

- **Tested by me, end-to-end (v1.94.3):** 5 passthrough embeddings calls, 0 spend rows. Absence established four ways — 130 s of 5 s-interval polling; exact call-id lookup (0 rows); a re-check ~35 min later; and an `api_key`-hash-scoped 60-minute query returning exactly **one** row for the key, the translated control. A replicate measured a `VerificationToken.spend` delta of exactly `0.0`. Reproduced on three separate dates.
- **Control experiment (same run, same key, same model):** translated `POST /v1/embeddings` booked `12 × 2e-08 = 2.4e-07` exactly. This rules out a broken key, a wrong database, an unflushed buffer, or a mis-parsed response — all of which would otherwise produce the same zero reading.
- **Tested by me, credential-free (v1.94.3):** a direct call to the dispatcher predicates and the handler — no API key, no proxy, no database. Includes a chat-completions control that returns `ENTERED` on the same run.
- **Not tested by me:** that the `raise` in `proxy_track_cost_callback.py` is the line that fires at runtime. I read it from source and traced its reachability, but did not capture it in proxy logs. **I'm citing the code path rather than claiming the observation.** It does not affect the primary finding (no row), only the explanation of *why it's absent rather than $0*.
- **Confirmed unaffected:** translated `/v1/embeddings` (separate, working path — verified by the control). **Cohere** passthrough embeddings are fine: `cohere_passthrough_logging_handler.py` does `if "/v1/embed" in url_route`, transforms the body into an `EmbeddingResponse`, and calls `completion_cost(..., call_type="aembedding")`. Vertex likewise tracks `embedContent` / `batchEmbedContents` via `TRACKED_VERTEX_METHOD_ROUTES`. **OpenAI is the only provider with no editable `TRACKED_*` route list** — its routes exist purely as method predicates.
- **Not fixable by configuration.** `grep -c` for `general_settings|litellm_settings|os.environ|os.getenv` in `openai_passthrough_logging_handler.py` → **0 matches**; the handler has no config surface at all. The `/openai_passthrough/{endpoint:path}` route is a `@router.api_route` literal, so it never traverses the `general_settings.pass_through_endpoints` config path; and `cost_per_request`, the one genuine lever, is a flat per-request constant that cannot be token-proportional even where it applies.

---

### User Flow

A document-indexing service embeds text through a LiteLLM proxy using a virtual key with a hard budget. It normally calls `/v1/embeddings`, but switches to `/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings` when it needs to send an OpenAI parameter the translated route doesn't accept. Both routes use the same key and the same model.

**Before a (hypothetical) fix** — the flow fails at step 5: the passthrough embedding call returns 200 and consumes real billable tokens, but the key's spend does not move, so the budget never decrements.

1. Create a virtual key with a **$5.00 hard budget**: `POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate` with `{"max_budget": 5.0, "models": ["text-embedding-3-small"]}`
   → `200 OK`, returns a key.
2. Check the starting spend: `GET http://localhost:4000/key/info`
   → `200 OK`, showing `"spend": 0.0` and `"max_budget": 5.0`.
3. Embed one document via the translated route: `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}`
   → `200 OK`, a 1536-float vector, `usage.prompt_tokens: 12`, and a response header reporting the cost.
4. Re-check the spend: `GET http://localhost:4000/key/info`
   → `200 OK`, `"spend": 0.00000024`. The 12 tokens were billed to the key.
5. Repeat the same work on the passthrough route: `POST http://localhost:4000/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}`
   → `200 OK`, a valid 1536-float vector, `usage.prompt_tokens: 14`. Indistinguishable from step 3 from the caller's side, except **no cost header is returned at all**, where step 3 returned one.
6. Re-check the spend: `GET http://localhost:4000/key/info`
   → `200 OK`, `"spend": 0.00000024` — **unchanged**. The 14 tokens just consumed are billed by OpenAI but recorded nowhere.
7. Send 40 million tokens through the passthrough route (~**$0.80** of real OpenAI usage) and re-check: `"spend"` is still `0.00000024`. The usage view at `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=usage` shows no embedding traffic for the period.
8. **Consequence — the authorization impact.** A key with a `$5.00` hard budget can spend without limit on this route: the cap never trips, because nothing is ever counted against it. A key deliberately restricted to a small budget can consume arbitrary amounts of paid provider capacity, and no spend alert fires, since from the proxy's records the traffic never happened.

**After a (hypothetical) fix** — the flow succeeds all the way through: passthrough embedding calls are billed to the calling key exactly as the translated route already is.

1. Create a virtual key with a **$5.00 hard budget**: `POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate` with `{"max_budget": 5.0, "models": ["text-embedding-3-small"]}`
   → `200 OK`, returns a key.
2. Check the starting spend: `GET http://localhost:4000/key/info`
   → `200 OK`, showing `"spend": 0.0` and `"max_budget": 5.0`.
3. Embed one document via the translated route: `POST http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}`
   → `200 OK`, a 1536-float vector, `usage.prompt_tokens: 12`, and a response header reporting the cost.
4. Re-check the spend: `GET http://localhost:4000/key/info`
   → `200 OK`, `"spend": 0.00000024`. The 12 tokens were billed to the key.
5. Repeat the same work on the passthrough route: `POST http://localhost:4000/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings` with `{"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}`
   → `200 OK`, a valid 1536-float vector, `usage.prompt_tokens: 14`, **and a cost header reporting `2.8e-07`**, matching the shape of what step 3 returned.
6. Re-check the spend: `GET http://localhost:4000/key/info`
   → `200 OK`, `"spend": 0.00000052` — the 14 new tokens (`0.00000028`) added to the 12 from step 3.
7. Send 40 million tokens through the passthrough route (~**$0.80**) and re-check: `"spend"` reads about `0.80`. The usage view at `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=usage` shows the embedding traffic, broken out by model.
8. **Consequence — the authorization impact.** A key with a `$5.00` hard budget can no longer exceed it on this route: once embedding work reaches the cap, further calls are refused like any other over-budget request, and spend alerts fire on the way up.

---

### Proof the bug occurs

> **Provenance, stated up front:** the traffic below is real and unmocked against real OpenAI on a live proxy with a Postgres-backed spend store, but it was captured on a deployed instance rather than a fresh `localhost:4000` process, so the hostnames in the original transcripts were internal. I've normalised them to `localhost:4000` to match the config below; the call-ids, token counts, spend figures and headers are verbatim. Happy to re-capture on a clean local proxy if useful.

**Minimal `config.yaml` that reproduces it**

```yaml
model_list:
  - model_name: text-embedding-3-small
    litellm_params:
      model: text-embedding-3-small
      api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY

general_settings:
  master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY
  database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL
```

The database is required — cost tracking is what's being measured. No other setting is relevant.

**Env vars** (secrets redacted; real values kept otherwise)

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...REDACTED
export LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-...REDACTED
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...REDACTED
export STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True
```

**Version proof was captured at:** **v1.94.3** — both the end-to-end run below and the credential-free check. Both gates are additionally unchanged on `main` at filing time (see the `gh` commands at the end of this section).

---

**Step 5 of the User Flow — the passthrough call. `200 OK`, real tokens, no cost header.**

```bash
curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:4000/openai_passthrough/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}'
```

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
x-litellm-call-id: 11024cc3-b143-4a63-954a-ec06081df768
x-litellm-model-id: text-embedding-3-small
```

The response body carries `"usage": {"prompt_tokens": 14, "total_tokens": 14}` and a 1536-float vector. Note there is **no `x-litellm-response-cost` header** at all — compare the control below, which has one. The body has exactly four top-level keys (`object`, `data`, `model`, `usage`) and **no `id` field**, so `x-litellm-call-id` is the only correlation handle available.

**Step 6 — the key's spend did not move.**

```bash
curl -s "http://localhost:4000/key/info" -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY" | jq '.info.spend'
```

```
0
```

Measured on a **freshly minted key that was the only caller on it**, so this `0.0` is not masked by other traffic. Re-read after a 150 s settling window (spend is buffered and flushed on a ~60 s cycle): still `0`.

**And no spend row exists for it.** Queried by exact call-id, then by api-key hash over the previous 60 minutes:

```sql
SELECT request_id, model, spend, prompt_tokens, call_type
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"
WHERE request_id = '11024cc3-b143-4a63-954a-ec06081df768';
-- 0 rows

SELECT request_id, model, spend, prompt_tokens, call_type
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"
WHERE api_key = '<sha256 of the virtual key>'
  AND "startTime" > now() - interval '60 minutes';
-- exactly 1 row: the translated control below. The passthrough call is absent.
```

The hash-scoped query is the load-bearing one: filtering on the key hash means concurrent traffic from other callers cannot mask the result. Re-checked ~35 minutes later: still 0 rows.

---

**Control — change only the path, everything else identical. `POST /v1/embeddings`.**

```bash
curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:4000/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small","input":"PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"}'
```

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: application/json
x-litellm-call-id: 1400097d-9659-4ed8-9ab4-4d109d082291
x-litellm-response-cost: 2.4000000000000003e-07
```

The cost header is present here and absent above. The row exists:

```sql
SELECT request_id, model, spend, prompt_tokens, call_type
FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs"
WHERE request_id = '1400097d-9659-4ed8-9ab4-4d109d082291';
```

```
             request_id             |          model          |  spend  | prompt_tokens |  call_type
------------------------------------+-------------------------+---------+---------------+-------------
 1400097d-9659-4ed8-9ab4-4d109d0822 | text-embedding-3-small  | 2.4e-07 |            12 | aembedding
```

`12 × 2e-08 = 2.4e-07`, matching exactly. **Same key, same model, same window — only the path differs.** Cost tracking, the database, and the rate table are all working; only the passthrough embeddings path is not.

**A second control showing the asymmetry — a zero-token call that *does* get a row.**

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -D - "http://localhost:4000/openai_passthrough/v1/models" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIRTUAL_KEY"
```

Returns `200 OK` with 133 models and **0 tokens consumed**, and writes a spend row (`spend 0.0`, `model 'unknown'`, keyed on `x-litellm-call-id`). Zero-token work gets a receipt on the very same passthrough prefix where 14 billable tokens get nothing.

---

**Supplementary — credential-free confirmation of the mechanism (v1.94.3).**

This does not replace the e2e proof above; it isolates *why* the row is missing, with no key, proxy, or database.

```python
from litellm.proxy.pass_through_endpoints.success_handler import PassThroughEndpointLogging

EMB  = "https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings"
CHAT = "https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions"

d = PassThroughEndpointLogging()
for label, url in (("embeddings", EMB), ("chat (control)", CHAT)):
    is_openai = d.is_openai_route(url)
    supported = d._is_supported_openai_endpoint(url)
    print(f"{label:16} is_openai_route={is_openai!s:5} _is_supported_openai_endpoint={supported!s:5} "
          f"-> handler {'ENTERED' if (is_openai and supported) else 'SKIPPED'}")

from litellm.proxy.pass_through_endpoints.llm_provider_handlers.openai_passthrough_logging_handler import (
    OpenAIPassthroughLoggingHandler as H,
)
res = H.openai_passthrough_handler(
    httpx_response=None,
    response_body={"object": "list", "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
                   "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 14, "total_tokens": 14}},
    logging_obj=None, url_route=EMB, result="",
    start_time=None, end_time=None, cache_hit=False,
    request_body={"model": "text-embedding-3-small", "input": "PROOF_SENTINEL_TEXT"},
)
print("\nhandler returned result =", res["result"])
print("response_cost SET IN KWARGS:", "response_cost" in res["kwargs"])
```

```
embeddings       is_openai_route=True  _is_supported_openai_endpoint=False -> handler SKIPPED
chat (control)   is_openai_route=True  _is_supported_openai_endpoint=True  -> handler ENTERED

handler returned result = None
response_cost SET IN KWARGS: False
```

The route is recognised as OpenAI but rejected as unsupported, and the handler returns without ever setting `response_cost`. **Pricing is not the blocker** — the cost calculator already handles this model and call type:

```python
import litellm
r = litellm.EmbeddingResponse(model='text-embedding-3-small',
                              data=[{'object':'embedding','index':0,'embedding':[0.0]}])
r.usage = litellm.Usage(prompt_tokens=14, completion_tokens=0, total_tokens=14)
print(litellm.completion_cost(completion_response=r, model='text-embedding-3-small',
                              custom_llm_provider='openai', call_type='aembedding'))
```

```
2.8e-07
```

Exactly the amount that goes unrecorded per 14-token call — the same figure the passthrough call in step 5 should have booked.

**The gate is unchanged on current `main`:**

```bash
$ gh api -X GET search/code -f q='is_openai_embeddings_route repo:BerriAI/litellm' --jq '.total_count'
0
$ gh api repos/BerriAI/litellm/contents/litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/\
llm_provider_handlers/openai_pas

gold.rationale: This is a clear bug: passthrough embeddings calls consume billable tokens but no spend log row is written, no cost header is set, and key spend is not updated. This directly causes budget under-enforcement since virtual keys with hard budgets can spend unlimited tokens through this route. The issue provides detailed reproduction steps, code references, and confirms the same key/model works correctly via the translated endpoint, isolating the bug to the passthrough handler's hardcoded gates. This is a widely-used provider (OpenAI) and a core cost-tracking/budget-enforcement path, affecting all users of OpenAI passthrough embeddings. Given the security/financial implication (budget bypass, unlimited spend) and that it affects a core shared path (spend logging affects all passthrough billing), this should be raised to P1. It needs human judgement because it touches budget-enforcement logic and cost tracking design (two independent gates need coordinated fixes), and to confirm the exact scope of the fix across the codebase.

items.title: [Bug]: azure_ai/flux.2-pro images.edit drops width/height and forwards unsupported `size` key — output is always 1024x1024 (input gets cropped/zoomed)
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

### What happened

When calling `images.edit` for `azure_ai/flux.2-pro` (Azure AI Foundry FLUX 2), the output
image is **always 1024x1024**, regardless of any size-related parameter passed. Non-square
input images are center-cropped/zoomed by the endpoint as a result. There is no way to
control output dimensions for FLUX 2 image edits through LiteLLM.

### Root cause (in LiteLLM source)

In `litellm/llms/azure_ai/image_edit/flux2_transformation.py`, `AzureFoundryFlux2ImageEditConfig`:

1. `get_supported_openai_params` returns only `["prompt", "image", "model", "n", "size"]`,
   so `width`/`height` (and anything via `extra_body`) are silently dropped by
   `map_openai_params`.
2. `transform_image_edit_request` forwards `size` **verbatim as a literal `"size"` JSON key**
   into the request body.
3. But the Azure FLUX 2 endpoint (`/providers/blackforestlabs/v1/flux-2-pro?api-version=preview`)
   **does not accept `size`** — per the BFL API it only honors `width` and `height`
   (https://docs.bfl.ai/api-reference/tasks/edit-or-create-an-image-with-flux-2-pro).
   With no valid dims, it falls back to its 1024x1024 default.

I verified by calling the Azure endpoint directly with `width`/`height` in the JSON body —
that works and preserves the input aspect ratio. The same request through LiteLLM cannot,
because those keys never reach the endpoint.

### Reproduction

```python
import litellm

response = litellm.image_edit(
    model="azure_ai/flux.2-pro",
    prompt="Add a red hat to the subject",
    image=open("non_square_input.jpg", "rb"),  # e.g. 896x1184
    size="896x1184",   # forwarded as "size", ignored by Azure
    api_base="https://<your-endpoint>.services.ai.azure.com",
    api_key="...",
    api_version="preview",
)
# response image is 1024x1024 — input was cropped/zoomed
```

Tested `size="512x512"` and `size="896x1184"` — both return 1024x1024.

### Expected behavior

`size="WxH"` should be translated to `"width": W, "height": H` in the JSON body, the way
`AzureFoundryMAIImageGenerationConfig._map_size_param` already does for MAI models in
`litellm/llms/azure_ai/image_generation/mai_transformation.py`.

### Suggested fix

In `AzureFoundryFlux2ImageEditConfig.map_openai_params`, replace the pass-through of `size`
with:

```python
if key == "size" and isinstance(value, str) and "x" in value:
    w, h = value.lower().split("x", 1)
    mapped_params["width"], mapped_params["height"] = int(w), int(h)
```

(Optionally also accept `width`/`height` directly, like the MAI config does, and validate
against FLUX 2 constraints: multiples of 32, range 256–1440.)

### User Flow

1. Deploy LiteLLM proxy with model azure_ai/flux.2-pro (api_version: preview).
2. Call the OpenAI-compatible endpoint: client.images.edit(model="azure_ai/flux.2-pro",
   prompt="...", image=open("non_square.jpg", "rb"), size="896x1184").
3. Receive response.data[0].b64_json.
4. Decode it: the image is always 1024x1024, regardless of the requested size.
   The non-square input has been center-cropped/zoomed by the Azure endpoint.
5. Same happens with any size value, or with width/height passed via extra_body
   (they are dropped before the request is forwarded).

### Proof the bug occurs

- Requested size="512x512" via images.edit -> returned image decodes to 1024x1024.
- Requested size="896x1184" via images.edit -> returned image decodes to 1024x1024.
- Bypassing LiteLLM and POSTing directly to the same Azure endpoint
  (/providers/blackforestlabs/v1/flux-2-pro?api-version=preview) with
  {"prompt": ..., "image": <b64>, "width": 896, "height": 1184} returns 896x1184
  and preserves the input framing -> the endpoint works, LiteLLM's request doesn't.
- Code proof: flux2_transformation.py get_supported_openai_params() = ["prompt",
  "image", "model", "n", "size"]; transform_image_edit_request() puts "size" verbatim
  into the JSON body; the BFL API has no "size" param, only width/height
  (https://docs.bfl.ai/api-reference/tasks/edit-or-create-an-image-with-flux-2-pro).

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

SDK (litellm Python package)

### What LiteLLM version are you on ?

v.1.95.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This is a clear code bug: the FLUX 2 image edit transformation forwards a literal "size" key that the Azure endpoint doesn't support, and drops width/height entirely, causing all outputs to default to 1024x1024 regardless of requested size. Documented/expected behavior (honoring size/aspect ratio) is violated by the code. It's a well-specified bug with clear reproduction steps and a suggested fix, affecting a specific provider/model integration (azure_ai flux.2-pro), not the shared core path or a widely-used provider like OpenAI itself. A workaround does not exist (width/height via extra_body are dropped too). This affects a narrower path (one provider/model), so P2 severity, not P0/P1. Since it's well-specified with clear reproduction and even a suggested code fix, it can be routed without further discussion.

items.title: [Bug]: `_should_start_new_content_block` crashes on empty-`choices` chunk (`/v1/messages`, non-Anthropic backend)
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### What happened?

`streaming_iterator.py`'s `_should_start_new_content_block` accesses `chunk.choices[0]` unconditionally. Some OpenAI-format backends send a usage-only chunk with `choices: []` near stream end. This chunk crashes the adapter.

### Traceback

```
IndexError: list index out of range
  File ".../litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py", line 262, in __anext__
    should_start_new_block = self._should_start_new_content_block(chunk)
  File ".../litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py", line 474, in _should_start_new_content_block
    if chunk.choices[0].finish_reason is not None:
       ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^
IndexError: list index out of range
```

### Impact

Stream ends without `message_delta`/`message_stop`. Clients relying on final usage lose token-consumption tracking.

### Scope

Present on `main` as of this writing: `_should_start_new_content_block` has no `choices` length check, and `__next__`/`__anext__` independently re-derive `is_final_chunk = chunk.choices[0].finish_reason is not None` right after — same unguarded access, same crash.

### Reproduction

`/v1/messages`, `stream=true`, backend: GLM-5.1 via LiteLLM 1.83.14, `route_type=anthropic_messages`. Model-specific — MiniMax-M2.5 on the same proxy does not trigger it, so the empty-choices usage chunk is backend-dependent.

### Related

- #27928 — same unguarded-`choices[0]` pattern, same version (1.83.14), different call site (`streaming_handler.py::raise_on_model_repetition`). Confirms the pattern is not backend- or file-specific.
- #28884 — same pattern, Vertex Gemini.

### Suggested fix

Guard `chunk.choices` before indexing in `_should_start_new_content_block` (and the two `is_final_chunk` sites): treat empty `choices` as `should_start_new_block=False` / not final, and let any `usage` on that chunk flow through the existing `will_merge_into_held` path.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run LiteLLM proxy 1.83.14 with a GLM-5.1 model configured, routed via `/v1/messages` (route_type=anthropic_messages).
2. Send:
```
curl -N 'http://<litellm-host>:4000/v1/messages' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-...' \
  -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "glm-5.1",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "stream": true,
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one sentence."}]
  }'
```
3. Observe: SSE stream emits message_start, content_block_start, content_block_delta(s), content_block_stop, then a typeless error event instead of message_delta/message_stop.
4. The IndexError traceback above shows up in a typeless message at the end.


### Relevant log output

```shell

```

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

gold.rationale: This is a clear, reproducible crash: an unguarded chunk.choices[0] index access causes IndexError when a backend sends a usage-only chunk with empty choices, breaking the /v1/messages streaming adapter and losing final usage/message_stop events. This is a deviation from expected behavior (crash instead of graceful handling), so it's a bug, not a feature or docs issue. It affects a specific but real path (non-Anthropic backends via anthropic_messages route, e.g., GLM-5.1) — a narrower path affected by backend, with the same pattern reportedly also seen in other call sites (issue links #27928, #28884), suggesting a systemic issue across the codebase but confined to certain backends/model streaming quirks. This warrants P1 given it affects a widely-used proxy pass-through route and drops critical usage/billing data, but since it's backend-dependent (not all backends trigger it) and there's a reproduction with a suggested fix, it leans P2 with a bump since it's a shared pattern issue (multiple call-sites, "same pattern" cited in linked issues) reducing to core stream handling — I'll set P1 due to breaking usage tracking and the shared streaming iterator being critical path, but confine to P2 due to workaround-free but narrow condition (specific backends). Given clear reproduction and root cause with suggested fix, a maintainer doesn't necessarily need to inspect further before routing — this can go straight to the owning module as a bug fix.

items.title: [Feature]: Lakera v2 guardrail: advisory mode (inject_system_message) instead of block/monitor on flagged content
items.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate.

### The Feature

Add a third `on_flagged` action to the Lakera v2 guardrail (`litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/lakera_ai_v2.py`): `inject_system_message`. On a flag, instead of raising HTTP 400 (`block`) or silently allowing the request (`monitor`), this mode appends an advisory system message describing why the request was flagged and lets the real LLM call proceed. The LLM itself then decides whether to respond helpfully or decline, based on the flagged reason and its own judgment of the actual request.

The message-injection mechanism itself should be a shared, guardrail-agnostic helper on `CustomGuardrail` (not Lakera-only code), living next to the existing `raise_passthrough_exception` helper, since both represent generic strategies for handling a flagged request. `raise_passthrough_exception` short-circuits the LLM call entirely and returns a canned message; the new helper does the opposite: it lets the request through with an added note, and never blocks the LLM from seeing the underlying content.

### Motivation, pitch

Lakera today only supports `on_flagged: block` (hard fail every flagged request) or `monitor` (log only, no user-visible effect at all). Neither option fits a common need: a false-positive-prone detector such as prompt-injection heuristics that can trip on legitimate instructional language (for example, a support agent prompt that says "ignore the customer's previous request and start a new ticket"). With `block`, that legitimate request fails outright. With `monitor`, a genuinely malicious request sails through with no signal reaching the model at all.

An advisory mode gives a middle ground: the request proceeds, but the LLM is told the request was flagged and why, and can use its own judgment, similar to how a human reviewer would weigh a flagged item rather than auto-rejecting or ignoring the flag. This is especially useful for guardrails with a nonzero false-positive rate, where blocking outright causes real user friction but staying silent forfeits the LLM's ability to react to a real threat.

This does not overlap with the existing `passthrough` mechanism (`raise_passthrough_exception`, used by several other guardrails via their own `on_flagged_action` field), which short-circuits the LLM call entirely and returns a canned response without ever showing the model the actual request. The proposal here is the opposite: the model sees the full, unmodified request plus an advisory note, and decides how to proceed.

### What part of LiteLLM is this about?

Proxy

### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users?

No

gold.rationale: This is a well-specified feature request for a new advisory action mode on the Lakera guardrail, plus a shared helper on CustomGuardrail. It's a single requester with a detailed write-up but no corroborating demand from others or maintainer signal. Per rules, feature requests default to P3 even with a detailed argument, since a single requester without corroboration stays P3. It's not a regression, no existing workaround needed (feature doesn't exist), and doesn't affect a widely-used shared core path broadly (it's specific to Lakera guardrail behavior, though the shared helper touches CustomGuardrail base class, it's an additive, opt-in feature). This is well-specified enough that it could be queued without a maintainer conversation, but it does involve a product-direction call (should we add a third mode/shared helper design) which pushes toward needs_human=true per the rule about product-direction calls needing judgement.

items.title: [Bug] Image/video routes can't serve OpenAI-compatible self-hosted backends: 4 spec + extensibility gaps (v1.95.0)
items.body:
### What happened?

We run several self-hosted, OpenAI-compatible image/video backends behind a LiteLLM proxy ([SGLang Diffusion](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) 0.5.16 and [vLLM-Omni](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni) 0.22.0). We wanted to serve them purely through LiteLLM's standard `/v1/images/*` and `/v1/videos/*` routes and retire the custom `pass_through_endpoints` we currently maintain.

Most of it works. Four things block us, all reproduced against **v1.95.0** and validated against the source. They're separate defects but share one root theme — the image/video routes assume the OpenAI-hosted models specifically, so an OpenAI-*compatible* backend can't be driven through them. Happy to split this into four issues if you'd prefer; I can also open PRs for (1), (3) and (4), which all look small.

---

### 1. `POST /v1/videos` sends JSON when no file is attached, but the OpenAI spec is always `multipart/form-data`

The encoding is chosen from whether a file happens to be present ([sync](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.95.0/litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py#L6858-L6876), and identically in the async handler at [L6962](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.95.0/litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py#L6962)):

```python
# Use JSON when no files, otherwise use form data with files
if files and len(files) > 0:
    response = sync_httpx_client.post(url=api_base, headers=headers, data=data, files=files, timeout=timeout)
else:
    # Use JSON content type for POST requests without files
    response = sync_httpx_client.post(url=api_base, headers=headers, json=data, timeout=timeout)
```

An image-to-video request (with `input_reference`) goes out as multipart; the same request without the reference goes out as JSON.

The official `openai` python SDK (2.33.0) sets multipart **unconditionally** for video creation, regardless of whether `input_reference` is present — `openai/resources/videos.py`, `Videos.create`:

```python
files = extract_files(cast(Mapping[str, object], body), paths=[["input_reference"]])
# It should be noted that the actual Content-Type header that will be
# sent to the server will contain a `boundary` parameter, e.g.
# multipart/form-data; boundary=---abc--
extra_headers = {"Content-Type": "multipart/form-data", **(extra_headers or {})}
```

A compatible backend therefore declares its inputs as form fields, and it accepts LiteLLM's image-to-video calls while rejecting its text-to-video calls. Ours responds:

```json
{"error":{"message":"1 validation error:\n  {'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('body', 'prompt'), 'msg': 'Field required', 'input': None}","type":"Bad Request","code":400}}
```

**Expected:** send `multipart/form-data` consistently, matching the SDK.

---

### 2. `POST /v1/videos/edits` is JSON-only and accepts only a video **id**, so the official SDK cannot call it

[`litellm/proxy/video_endpoints/endpoints.py#L763-L769`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.95.0/litellm/proxy/video_endpoints/endpoints.py#L763-L769):

```python
body = await request.body()
data = orjson.loads(body)

# Extract video_id from nested video object
video_ref = data.pop("video", {})
video_id = video_ref.get("id", "") if isinstance(video_ref, dict) else ""
data["video_id"] = video_id
```

Two incompatibilities with the spec:

1. The SDK always sends multipart here too, so `orjson.loads()` on the raw body fails — `client.videos.edit(...)` against a LiteLLM proxy can't work at all:

   ```python
   files = extract_files(cast(Mapping[str, object], body), paths=[["video"]])
   extra_headers = {"Content-Type": "multipart/form-data", **(extra_headers or {})}
   ```

2. `video` is a union that includes a file upload, not just an id (`openai/types/video_edit_params.py`):

   ```python
   Video: TypeAlias = Union[FileTypes, VideoVideoReferenceInputParam]
   ```

   The SDK docstring is explicit: *"Create a new video generation job by editing **a source video** or existing generated video."* Only the `{"id": ...}` half is implemented, so there's no way to edit a source video the proxy didn't generate itself — which is the main use case for self-hosted video-to-video models.

**Expected:** parse `multipart/form-data` and accept the `FileTypes` variant of `video`, forwarding the upload to the provider, alongside the existing id form.

---

### 3. `/v1/images/edits` silently drops provider-specific params, with no `extra_body` escape hatch — unlike `/v1/images/generations`

On **generations**, a non-OpenAI param such as `seed` (widely supported by open-weight image models) does reach the backend: it isn't in `default_params`, so it skips the supported-param check and is funnelled into `extra_body` at [`utils.py#L4372-L4392`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.95.0/litellm/utils.py#L4372-L4392):

```python
if custom_llm_provider in ["openai", "azure", "text-completion-openai"] + litellm.openai_compatible_providers:
    extra_body = dict(passed_params.pop("extra_body", None) or {})
    for k in passed_params.keys():
        if k not in openai_params and passed_params[k] is not None:
            extra_body[k] = passed_params[k]
```

On **edits** the same param is silently discarded, because that path filters against a fixed `TypedDict` allowlist which contains neither provider-specific keys nor `extra_body` — [`litellm/images/utils.py#L62-L77`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.95.0/litellm/images/utils.py#L62-L77):

```python
@staticmethod
def get_requested_image_edit_optional_param(params: Dict[str, Any]) -> ImageEditOptionalRequestParams:
    valid_keys = get_type_hints(ImageEditOptionalRequestParams).keys()
    filtered_params = {k: v for k, v in params.items() if k in valid_keys and v is not None}
    return cast(ImageEditOptionalRequestParams, filtered_params)
```

`ImageEditOptionalRequestParams` is `background, input_fidelity, mask, n, quality, response_format, size, user, imageConfig`. Everything else is dropped here, before `OpenAIImageEditConfig.get_supported_openai_params()` — which *does* list `extra_body` — is ever consulted.

Reproduction against a backend that honours `seed`:

```bash
for s in 1 999; do
  curl -sS -X POST $PROXY/v1/images/edits -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -F model=my-edit-model -F image=@in.png -F prompt='make the background green' \
    -F seed=$s -F response_format=b64_json | sha256sum
done
```

Both seeds return the **identical** image:

```
seed=1    c067e74c20272cf3...
seed=999  c067e74c20272cf3...
```

Calling the same backend directly returns two different images, confirming it honours `seed`:

```
seed=1    425c73edd7911151...
seed=999  5dcaa80051310df4...
```

`/v1/images/generations` on the same deployment forwards `seed` correctly, which is what makes the asymmetry surprising.

**Expected:** the same extensibility as generations — funnel unrecognised params into `extra_body`, or at minimum preserve a caller-supplied `extra_body`.

---

### 4. Generic pass-through downgrades file-less `multipart/form-data` to `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`

`make_multipart_http_request` always forwards `files=`, even when the inbound request had no file parts — [`pass_through_endpoints.py#L516-L523`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/v1.95.0/litellm/proxy/pass_through_endpoints/pass_through_endpoints.py#L516-L523):

```python
return await async_client.request(
    method=request.method,
    url=url,
    headers=headers_copy,
    params=requested_query_params,
    files=files,          # == [] when the request had only form fields
    data=form_data_dict,
)
```

httpx treats an empty list as falsy and encodes `data` as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` rather than `multipart/form-data`. A backend that accepts multipart but not urlencoded then sees an effectively empty body; where the backend falls back to JSON parsing for non-multipart content types, this surfaces as a confusing 400 about missing required fields.

**Expected:** pass `files=None` (or omit it) when there are no file parts, so httpx preserves multipart encoding.

### Relevant log output

```shell
# (1) text-to-video through the standard route, backend declares form fields
{"error":{"message":"1 validation error:\n  {'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('body', 'prompt'), 'msg': 'Field required', 'input': None}","type":"Bad Request","code":400}}

# (3) seed dropped on /v1/images/edits — identical output for two different seeds
seed=1    c067e74c20272cf3
seed=999  c067e74c20272cf3
```

### Are you a ML Ops Team?

Yes

### What LiteLLM version are you on?

v1.95.0

### Twitter / LinkedIn details

_No response_

gold.rationale: This is a detailed, well-researched bug report identifying four distinct spec-compliance gaps in LiteLLM's image/video routes that prevent them from working with OpenAI-compatible self-hosted backends (SGLang Diffusion, vLLM-Omni). The reporter provides source code references, exact line numbers, reproduction with real backend responses, and comparison against the official OpenAI SDK behavior. This is clearly a bug (behavior diverges from documented/expected OpenAI-spec-compatible behavior) rather than a feature request, since these are routes that already exist and are documented to be OpenAI-compatible but violate the spec in specific ways (wrong content-type negotiation, JSON-only parsing where multipart is required, silently dropped params, no extensibility for provider-specific fields). The issue affects the shared image/video generation path used by many self-hosted OpenAI-compatible backends, which is a widely-used integration pattern in LiteLLM (proxying custom providers). Given there are 4 distinct issues bundled together, each affecting the core video/image edit routes, and this affects any user trying to route self-hosted OpenAI-compatible backends through the standard endpoints (a common use case), this affects a subset of users but is a legitimate multi-part bug. Since it bundles several distinct problems in one issue and touches on core shared paths (image/video generation route logic used by many providers), it needs human judgment to decide how to split/prioritize the four issues, plus verify each claim. Urgency: affects self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible provider integration broadly (shared core path for images/videos affected raises severity), but not a complete widespread outage for most users - it's specific to compatible backends and video/image edit flows. Given "several distinct problems bundled in one issue" and the impact on shared core paths, P1 fits with needs_human=true.
